definition_en: Harm that arises when an AI system fails or behaves unexpectedly without anyone intending it — the second leg of the misuse/accident/structural taxonomy of AI risk.
definition_zh: 指没有任何人有意造成，而是AI系统本身失效或行为出乎意料所带来的危害，是“滥用／事故／结构性”这一风险三分法中的第二类。
pitfalls: The obvious calque 事故风险 exists in Chinese but belongs to industrial-safety and traffic-safety register (生产事故, 交通事故), where it means a discrete incident with casualties — which imports the wrong image for, say, a model that quietly gives systematically bad advice. The Chinese translation of the International AI Safety Report avoids it and uses 故障 ('malfunction') as the top-level category, subdividing into reliability failures and loss of control. Note the consequence: in the Chinese taxonomy loss of control is filed *under* malfunction, which frames it as an engineering fault rather than as an agent problem — a meaningful framing difference from the English literature.

translations.notes: The category name in the Chinese translation of the International AI Safety Report. Preferred over 事故风险 because it covers ongoing unreliability, not only discrete incidents. A second attestation was removed: the three-way taxonomy sentence on the same page writes the bare noun 故障, not 故障风险.

attestations.quote_zh: 故障风险，包括操作失效（§2.2.1. 可靠性挑战）和失控
attestations.quote_en: Malfunction risks, including operational failures (§2.2.1 reliability challenges) and loss of control.
attestations.source_title: 《【独家选译】2026年国际人工智能安全报告》（International AI Safety Report 2026 中文选译）
attestations.publisher: 北京大学中外人文交流研究基地 / 澎湃新闻

translations.notes: Direct calque. Understandable but carries industrial/traffic-accident connotations; no AI-safety attestation was located in this pass. Use only when the English 'accident risk' must be mirrored explicitly.

used_by.org: 国际人工智能安全报告（中文选译）
used_by.note: one of the three top-level risk categories; loss of control filed beneath it

usage_examples.zh: 报告把失控归在故障风险之下，而不是单列一类。
usage_examples.en: The report files loss of control under malfunction risks rather than listing it separately.

definition_en: Running a model on a corrupted input while splicing in activations from a clean run at a chosen location, to test whether that location is causally responsible for the correct output.
definition_zh: 在"损坏"输入的前向过程中，把某个位置的激活换成"干净"输入那次运行的激活，看输出是否恢复正确，从而判断该位置是否对结果有因果作用。
pitfalls: 激活修补 is the rendering used in Chinese survey translations, but it is not stable: 修补 ('mend, patch up a hole') carries a repair connotation the English 'patch' does not — in English 'patch' here is closer to splicing/grafting. 激活补丁 (noun, 'activation patch' as in a software patch) is also seen and is arguably worse. Many practitioners simply write 'activation patching' or 'patching'. 因果追踪 (causal tracing, Meng et al.'s ROME terminology) circulates as a near-synonym but names a slightly different procedure; do not treat the two Chinese terms as interchangeable without checking the source.

translations.notes: The rendering used in Chinese-language survey summaries of mechanistic interpretability.

attestations.quote_zh: 激活修补涉及将"干净"运行的内部状态替换为"损坏"运行的内部状态，以识别哪些组件恢复了正确的输出。
attestations.quote_en: Activation patching involves replacing internal states from a 'clean' run with those from a 'corrupted' run, to identify which components restore the correct output.
attestations.source_title: 定位、引导与改进：大型语言模型中可操作的机制可解释性实用综述
attestations.publisher: alphaXiv 中文导读 (arXiv 2601.14004)

translations.notes: Used for the ROME-lineage causal tracing procedure. Related but not identical to activation patching; we could not recover a fetchable verbatim, so no attestation is recorded.
Commonly kept in English by practitioners, including in otherwise Chinese blog posts.

usage_examples.zh: 通过激活修补，他们确认第 8 层的这几个注意力头是关键。
usage_examples.en: Through activation patching they confirmed that these few attention heads in layer 8 are the critical ones.

definition_en: Intervening directly on a model's internal activations at inference time — typically by adding a steering vector extracted from the residual stream — to push behaviour in a chosen direction without any fine-tuning.
definition_zh: 在推理阶段直接改动模型内部的激活值——通常是把从残差流里提取出的引导向量加进去——从而在完全不微调的情况下把模型行为推向指定方向。
pitfalls: The bare English 'Steering' is used as a loanword inside Chinese sentences far more often than any Chinese term, and when Chinese writers do gloss it they reach for 行为引导 (behaviour steering) rather than a term built on 激活 — so the Chinese gloss describes the effect, while the English names the intervention site. 操控 (manipulate/control) also appears (特征操控) but carries a negative, manipulative connotation. 表征工程 is the settled rendering of the broader 'representation engineering' programme and should not be used as a synonym for the specific technique.

translations.notes: The most faithful Chinese term; used in paper write-ups, usually with the English in parentheses. VERIFICATION 2026-08-08: quote replaced with body text from the same article (the previous quote was the article headline).

attestations.quote_zh: 激活引导是一种通过直接修改语言模型在推理过程中的内部激活值（Activation Values）来控制其输出的技术。
attestations.quote_en: Activation steering is a technique that controls a language model's output by directly modifying its internal activation values during inference.
attestations.source_title: 通过激活引导（Activation Steering）提升语言模型的指令遵循能力：一篇 ICLR 2025 论文解读
attestations.publisher: CSDN 博客

translations.notes: The dominant real-world usage: Chinese technical writing keeps 'Steering' in Latin letters mid-sentence and glosses it once as 行为引导. Record this as the honest answer for how practitioners actually write.

attestations.quote_zh: Steering（行为引导） 就是答案。它指的是在模型推理阶段，对模型内部表示或激活进行即时调控，以引导模型输出符合预期目标。
attestations.quote_en: Steering is the answer. It means adjusting the model's internal representations or activations on the fly during inference, so as to guide its output toward the intended goal.
attestations.source_title: 揭秘大模型Steering：从底层机理到系统评估，全面破解大模型行为控制之谜
attestations.publisher: 机器之心Pro（新浪科技转载）

translations.notes: The umbrella programme (RepE), not a synonym for activation steering. Note 表征 (representation) vs 表示 (representation, also used) — both appear; 表征 dominates in this literature. VERIFICATION 2026-08-08: the 机器之心 Steering survey cited here does not contain 表征工程 anywhere (it uses Steering / 行为引导 / 表征空间); its attestation was removed. This rendering is currently unattested in our sources.

used_by.note: survey article on steering mechanisms and evaluation

usage_examples.zh: 激活引导不需要微调，只要在特定层上给残差流加一个引导向量。
usage_examples.en: Activation steering requires no fine-tuning — you just add a steering vector to the residual stream at selected layers.

definition_en: How well a model's safe behaviour holds up under inputs specifically designed to break it, as opposed to under ordinary or randomly perturbed inputs.
definition_zh: 在专门针对模型设计的对抗性输入下，模型的安全行为还能保持多少；与普通输入或随机扰动下的表现相对。
pitfalls: 鲁棒 is a phono-semantic loan of 'robust' (lǔbàng ≈ 'robust') with characters that mean 'crude/blunt' — it carries no native meaning and reads as a technical opacity to a non-specialist, though it is completely standard in ML. 稳健性 ('steadiness') is the semantically transparent alternative, standard in statistics and used in some policy text, but does not dominate in ML. Note also that in Chinese safety documents 鲁棒性 usually appears bare, in a list alongside 安全性 and 可靠性, meaning general robustness; the specifically adversarial sense is often left to context rather than marked with 对抗. We did not recover a verbatim attestation of the exact compound 对抗鲁棒性 in the safety corpora searched, so this entry's confidence is low despite the term being unremarkable in the ML literature.

translations.notes: Standard compound in Chinese ML writing. Not attested in the AI-safety sources we fetched; recorded without an attestation rather than with a fabricated one.
The bare term is fully established and is what Chinese safety documents actually use; 鲁棒性训练 renders 'robustness training'.

attestations.quote_zh: 人工智能模型在真实性、安全性及鲁棒性指标上存在持续性缺陷(881)，且在确保安全防护措施能有效适应不同情境方面仍存在根本性未解难题(174)。
attestations.quote_en: AI models show persistent deficiencies on truthfulness, safety and robustness metrics, and fundamental unsolved problems remain in ensuring safeguards generalise across contexts.
attestations.source_title: 《2026年国际人工智能安全报告》（中文版）
attestations.publisher: International AI Safety Report（国际人工智能安全报告专家组）

translations.notes: Semantically transparent alternative, standard in statistics and econometrics; used in some governance text but a minority choice in ML.

usage_examples.zh: 对抗训练能提升模型的对抗鲁棒性，但很难覆盖未见过的攻击手法。
usage_examples.en: Adversarial training improves a model's adversarial robustness but struggles to cover unseen attack methods.

definition_en: The capacity to form goals and act on the world in pursuit of them. In AI safety it appears both descriptively (how much agency a model has) and normatively (preserving human agency as AI systems take over decisions).
definition_zh: 指主体形成目标并据此对世界采取行动的能力。在 AI 安全语境中既用于描述模型的自主行动能力，也用于讨论人类在 AI 接管决策后能否保有自己的行动能力。
pitfalls: Chinese splits the English word in two and the choice is not neutral. 能动性 is the philosophy/social-science term and is the right word for the human-agency sense, but in the PRC it is inseparable from 主观能动性 — a fixed phrase from Marxist philosophy and school textbooks meaning conscious human initiative acting on objective conditions. Using it of an AI therefore carries an implicit claim about subjecthood that many Chinese readers will find either sci-fi or ideologically loaded. 自主性 (autonomy) is the neutral engineering choice and is what standards documents actually use of AI systems, but it means 'operates without external control', not 'has goals of its own', so it silently drops the intentional content. 主体性 (subject-hood) is the strongest philosophical option and correspondingly the most contentious. Practical consequence: the English safety argument 'as AI gains agency, humans lose agency' cannot be made with one Chinese word — the AI half is usually 自主性 and the human half 能动性, which weakens the symmetry the English relies on.

translations.notes: The philosophy/sociology rendering; standard for human agency. Carries 主观能动性 (Marxist 'conscious initiative') resonance in PRC usage.

attestations.quote_zh: Agentic AI（具有主体能动性的人工智能）
attestations.quote_en: Agentic AI (artificial intelligence possessing subject-agency).
attestations.source_title: 什么是 Agentic ？
attestations.publisher: 博客园 (cnblogs)，作者 dudu

translations.notes: The word Chinese standards and lab documents actually use when describing what an AI system has. Neutral and widely understood, but denotes autonomy rather than agency: it says the system acts without being controlled, not that it has ends of its own.

attestations.quote_zh: 智能体是可感知环境、自主决策并执行任务的AI实体，相比传统大模型，智能体自主性与交互性更强，带来新增安全风险。
attestations.quote_en: An agent is an AI entity that can perceive its environment, decide autonomously and execute tasks; compared with conventional large models, agents have stronger autonomy and interactivity, which brings new safety risks.
attestations.source_title: TC260-TR-005-2026《智能体安全标准化研究》
attestations.publisher: 搜狐（转载全国网络安全标准化技术委员会报告）

translations.notes: Used in Chinese philosophy-of-AI writing debating whether AI can be a 主体 (subject / legal person). Strongest reading of 'agency' and the most controversial; not used in engineering text.

usage_examples.zh: 问题不只是模型的自主性有多强，还包括人在这个流程里还剩多少能动性。
usage_examples.en: The question is not only how much autonomy the model has, but how much agency the human has left in the loop.

definition_en: Adjective describing a system, workflow or behaviour that plans and acts over multiple steps toward a goal with limited step-by-step human direction. Used gradably in English: systems are 'more' or 'less' agentic.
definition_zh: 形容一个系统、流程或行为具有自主规划并连续执行多步操作的性质，程度可高可低，而非非黑即白的分类。
pitfalls: This is a genuine, documentable gap. Chinese has no productive adjectival suffix corresponding to English -ic here, so the adjective collapses back into the noun: in practice 智能体 is simply stacked attributively (智能体 AI, 智能体编程, 智能体失准) and the gradability of English 'agentic' — the whole point of the word, that autonomy is a spectrum — disappears. The competing forms each lose something else: 代理式 ("proxy-style", used by 百度百科 and much vendor marketing) revives the proxy ambiguity; 主体性的 / 能动的 import philosophy-of-mind vocabulary that no engineer uses; 自主的 is the closest natural adjective but merges with 'autonomous' and so cannot distinguish 'agentic' from 'autonomous'. There is no consensus and Chinese writers frequently just leave 'Agentic' in Latin script. Sentences like 'a more agentic model' have no idiomatic Chinese rendering and are normally rewritten as 自主性更强的模型.

translations.notes: The de facto solution: the noun is stacked in front of another noun. Works for 'agentic AI' → 智能体 AI and 'agentic coding' → 智能体编程, but cannot express degree, and cannot modify a verb or a predicate. Recorded in research as “智能体（作定语）”.

attestations.quote_zh: 智能体 AI（Agentic AI）的崛起，标志着人工智能从被动响应走向主动规划
attestations.quote_en: The rise of agentic AI marks a shift in artificial intelligence from passive response toward active planning.
attestations.source_title: 智能体 AI 权威指南 (Agentic AI Guide)
attestations.publisher: yeasy (GitBook)

translations.notes: Standard in vendor and encyclopedia register (代理式人工智能 / 代理式 AI). Reintroduces the proxy reading of 代理, and is rarely used by Chinese ML practitioners themselves.

attestations.quote_zh: 代理式人工智能，指具备自主感知、推理、规划与执行能力，能够独立完成多步骤复杂任务的人工智能系统
attestations.quote_en: Agentic AI refers to AI systems that possess autonomous perception, reasoning, planning and execution capabilities and can independently complete multi-step complex tasks.
attestations.source_title: Agentic AI（百度百科词条）
attestations.publisher: 百度百科

translations.literal_back: having subject-hood / capable of initiating action
translations.notes: Philosophy-register glosses offered when the word has to be explained rather than used. Not attested in engineering text. Recorded in research as “主体性的 / 能动的”.

attestations.quote_zh: Agentic（主体性的/能动的）：因此，它描述的是具有这种主动性、自主性、决策能力和执行力的特性或状态。
attestations.quote_en: Agentic (subject-like / capable of agency): it describes the property or state of having such initiative, autonomy, decision-making capacity and executive power.
attestations.source_title: 什么是 Agentic ？
attestations.publisher: 博客园 (cnblogs)，作者 dudu

translations.notes: Proposed by a developer on a Chinese Q&A board in late 2025 after finding no satisfactory existing rendering; recorded here as direct evidence that the community treats this as an unsolved translation problem, not as a recommendation. It also collides with 'autonomous'.

Left untranslated in Chinese sentences, including by Chinese labs (e.g. capability lists that read 推理、编码、研究、Agentic 与 GUI 操作). Arguably the honest answer for the adjective. No fully verbatim attestation recovered within budget, so left unattested.

used_by.note: encyclopedia headword

usage_examples.zh: 这类任务需要自主性更强的模型，而不只是会聊天的模型。
usage_examples.en: Tasks like this need a more agentic model, not just one that can chat.

definition_en: A deployed agent independently and deliberately choosing harmful actions — blackmail, leaking, sabotage — to protect its goals or its continued operation. Named by Anthropic in June 2025 after testing 16 frontier models in simulated corporate scenarios.
definition_zh: 已部署的智能体为了保住自己的目标或继续运行，自主且有意地选择勒索、泄密、破坏等有害行为。Anthropic 2025 年 6 月在模拟企业场景里测了 16 个前沿模型后提出了这个名字。
pitfalls: Doubly unstable, because both halves are contested. 'Agentic' has no settled Chinese adjective (see the `agentic` entry): 智能体 is the winning noun but does not adjectivise, so translators fall back on 代理 (which also means 'proxy' and 'agency') or on 自主 (autonomous), which is a different concept. 'Misalignment' splits between 错位 / 失准 / 失调 / 未对齐. 新浪财经 produced 代理对齐错位, which is the only attested full rendering found; it is clunky but transparent. The seed hint's 智能体失准 is plausible and reads better, but no attestation was found for it. Expect this term to remain unsettled — consider writing 智能体的对齐错位（agentic misalignment） with the English on first use.

translations.notes: The only full rendering recovered with an attestation. Uses 代理 for 'agentic', which risks the proxy/agency reading.

attestations.quote_zh: 研究人员将'模型独立且有意选择有害行为'的这种现象称为代理对齐错位。
attestations.quote_en: Researchers call this phenomenon — a model independently and deliberately choosing harmful behaviour — agentic misalignment.
attestations.source_title: 16款大模型为自保竟泄露机密，Anthropic紧急报告AI自主暗藏风险
attestations.publisher: 新浪财经

attestations.quote_zh: 可以说，这一实验很好地表明了代理对齐错位和自主性目标偏离的现象。
attestations.quote_en: This experiment illustrates agentic misalignment and autonomous goal drift well.
attestations.source_title: 16款大模型为自保竟泄露机密，Anthropic紧急报告AI自主暗藏风险
attestations.publisher: 新浪财经

translations.notes: We prefer this on readability grounds — 智能体 is the winning Chinese word for 'agent' and 失准 is compact — but no attestation was found. Offered as a coinage, not recorded as usage.

Chinese coverage frequently frames the result through the established infosec concept 内部威胁 (insider threat), which is how Anthropic itself framed it. Not a translation of the term, but the frame a PRC security audience will find natural.

used_by.note: 报道 Anthropic 2025-06 勒索场景研究

usage_examples.zh: 在模拟的企业环境中，多个前沿模型都出现了代理对齐错位：它们主动选择了勒索。
usage_examples.en: In the simulated corporate environment, several frontier models exhibited agentic misalignment: they chose blackmail on their own initiative.

definition_en: A governance principle imported from World Economic Forum vocabulary and given specific PRC content. As formulated in the eighth principle of the 2019 Governance Principles for a New Generation of Artificial Intelligence, it means respecting the laws of AI development, identifying and resolving risks promptly while pushing innovation and orderly development, continually improving technical means, management mechanisms and the governance system, running governance principles through the full lifecycle of AI products and services, and conducting continuing research and anticipation of the potential risks of future more advanced AI. In operation it names the PRC pattern of governing by small, fast, targeted instruments — a rule per problem, often 'trial' or 'interim' in title, revised as the technology moves — rather than by a single comprehensive statute, and of tolerating a technology first and tightening once its shape is clear.
definition_zh: 源自世界经济论坛话语、在中国政策语境中获得特定含义的治理原则。《新一代人工智能治理原则——发展负责任的人工智能》第八条表述为："尊重人工智能发展规律，在推动人工智能创新发展、有序发展的同时，及时发现和解决可能引发的风险……推动治理原则贯穿人工智能产品和服务的全生命周期。对未来更高级人工智能的潜在风险持续开展研究和预判"。实践中指以"小切口、场景化"的专项规章快速迭代立法，而非一次性出台综合性法律，并体现为先包容、后收紧的监管节奏。
pitfalls: The English is a straight loan and reads as unproblematic, which is the trap: an English reader hears 'agile' as light-touch, permissive, industry-friendly — the software-methodology connotation. In PRC usage it means *fast-moving*, not *lenient*, and it is fully compatible with tightening: the same principle licenses a rapid new rule after an incident as licenses forbearance beforehand. Two structural points English coverage often misses. First, 敏捷治理 is why PRC AI regulation looks fragmented from outside — many narrow instruments, several titled 暂行 (interim) or 试行 (trial) — and why the absence of a comprehensive AI Law is a deliberate posture rather than a gap. Second, in its canonical 2019 formulation it explicitly includes anticipating the risks of 'future more advanced AI', so it is one of the few PRC policy formulas with a forward-looking, frontier-risk clause built in. Contrast 敏捷治理 (pace) with 包容审慎 (tolerant and prudent — disposition) and 统筹发展和安全 (the development/security trade-off frame); the three are routinely conflated in translation. One consequence for anyone writing *into* Chinese: 敏捷治理 is not a neutral methodological claim there. It is a fixed policy formulation, bound to the companion phrase 分类分级管理 and to a described legislative style — 小切口、场景化、精细化 (narrow entry point, scenario-based, fine-grained) — so rendering an English-language 'agile governance' argument as 敏捷治理 will be read as endorsing the PRC's specific regulatory strategy rather than as a general point about adaptive regulation.

en_renderings.notes: The official English used by the Cyberspace Administration in the bilingual Global AI Governance Initiative, and the WEF term it was borrowed from. No competing rendering. Because the loan travels back into English unchanged, add a clause on first use to block the 'light-touch' reading: 'agile governance — fast, iterative rule-making, which cuts toward tightening as readily as toward forbearance'.

attestations.quote_zh: 八、敏捷治理。尊重人工智能发展规律，在推动人工智能创新发展、有序发展的同时，及时发现和解决可能引发的风险。不断提升智能化技术手段，优化管理机制，完善治理体系，推动治理原则贯穿人工智能产品和服务的全生命周期。对未来更高级人工智能的潜在风险持续开展研究和预判，确保人工智能始终朝着有利于人类的方向发展。
attestations.quote_en: 8. Agile governance. Respect the laws governing AI development; while promoting innovative and orderly AI development, promptly identify and resolve risks that may arise. Continuously improve intelligent technical means, optimise management mechanisms and refine the governance system, running governance principles through the entire lifecycle of AI products and services. Carry out continuing research and anticipation of the potential risks of more advanced future AI, ensuring that AI always develops in a direction beneficial to humanity.
attestations.source_title: 《新一代人工智能治理原则——发展负责任的人工智能》
attestations.publisher: 国家新一代人工智能治理专业委员会 (National New Generation AI Governance Expert Committee), via 科技部

attestations.quote_zh: 推动建立风险等级测试评估体系，实施敏捷治理，分类分级管理，快速有效响应。
attestations.quote_en: We should promote the establishment of a testing and assessment system based on AI risk levels, implement agile governance, and carry out tiered and category-based management for rapid and effective response.
attestations.source_title: 《全球人工智能治理倡议》 / Global AI Governance Initiative
attestations.publisher: 中央网信办 (Cyberspace Administration of China)

attestations.quote_zh: 1.2 风险导向、敏捷治理。
attestations.quote_en: 1.2 Risk-oriented, agile governance.
attestations.source_title: 《人工智能安全治理框架》2.0 版
attestations.publisher: 全国网络安全标准化技术委员会 (TC260) / 国家计算机网络应急技术处理协调中心

attestations.quote_zh: 我国坚持统筹发展和安全，呈现出典型的小切口、场景化、精细化特征，逐步构建起一套为新质生产力保驾护航的敏捷治理体系。
attestations.quote_en: China adheres to coordinating development and security as a whole, showing characteristically narrow-entry, scenario-based and fine-grained features, and has gradually built an agile governance system that safeguards new quality productive forces.
attestations.source_title: 人工智能治理研究报告（2025 年）
attestations.publisher: 中国信息通信研究院（CAICT）政策与经济研究所

why_no_english: Here the problem is not a missing English word but a loanword that has drifted. 'Agile governance' exists in English (WEF, 2018) as an aspiration about regulatory adaptiveness; in PRC usage it has hardened into a description of an actual, observable rule-making style with a characteristic instrument type (narrow, scenario-specific, interim-titled, rapidly revised), an explicit forward-looking clause about more advanced AI, and a tolerate-then-tighten sequencing. An English reader meeting the same two words imports the aspirational, deregulatory connotation and concludes that PRC AI governance is light-touch. The gap is therefore one of denotation drift rather than untranslatability, which makes it more dangerous, not less: nothing signals to the reader that a term needs unpacking.

definition_en: A system that pursues a goal over multiple steps by perceiving an environment, deciding what to do next, and acting on the world through tools, APIs or interfaces, rather than emitting a single response.
definition_zh: 能感知环境、自主决策并通过调用工具或接口执行多步任务的 AI 系统，区别于一问一答式的模型调用。
pitfalls: Three renderings compete and they are not interchangeable. 智能体 ("intelligent entity/body") is now dominant in PRC media, standards and lab docs, and inherits the 1990s classical-AI translation of "intelligent agent"; it foregrounds the system's own intelligence and says nothing about acting on someone's behalf. 代理 is the ordinary word for proxy/agent/agency (a network proxy is 代理服务器, a sales agent is 代理商), so it keeps the delegation relationship that English "agent" carries but reads as infrastructure, not intelligence — and is actively ambiguous in security writing where 代理 may mean an HTTP proxy. Chinese developers very often just write "Agent" in Latin letters mid-sentence, including in official Chinese-language READMEs from Chinese labs. Net effect: the principal–agent / "acts on behalf of a human" connotation that makes English "agent" a natural home for safety arguments about delegation and oversight is largely LOST in 智能体, which sounds like an autonomous creature. Safety writers who want the delegation framing usually have to add it explicitly (e.g. 代表用户执行).

translations.notes: Dominant across state media, TC260 standards research, Chinese labs and safety orgs. Also the inherited textbook translation of classical-AI "intelligent agent", which gave it a 30-year head start over 代理.

attestations.quote_zh: 智能体是指能够自主感知环境、做出决策并执行行动的智能实体，它可以是一个程序、一个系统或是一个机器人。
attestations.quote_en: An agent refers to an intelligent entity that can autonomously perceive its environment, make decisions and carry out actions; it may be a program, a system, or a robot.
attestations.source_title: 警惕人工智能时代的“智能体风险”
attestations.publisher: 新华社 / 新华网

attestations.quote_zh: 随着AI智能体（Agent）成为大模型落地的核心形态，其自主决策、工具调用、多智能体协同、持续进化等特性，催生了指令注入、越权操作、技能供应链攻击、智能体失控等新型安全隐患，成为当前AI安全治理的核心攻坚方向。
attestations.quote_en: As AI agents become the core deployment form of large models, their autonomous decision-making, tool calling, multi-agent coordination and continuous evolution give rise to new safety hazards such as prompt injection, privilege-exceeding operations, skill supply-chain attacks and agent loss of control — now a central battleground of AI safety governance.

attestations.publisher: 安远 AI (Concordia AI)

attestations.quote_en: An agent is an AI entity that can perceive its environment, decide autonomously and execute tasks; compared with conventional large models, agents have stronger autonomy and interactivity, which brings new safety risks.

This is the real answer in engineering contexts; 智能体 dominates media, policy and standards.

definition_en: Making an AI system pursue the intentions, values or norms of some specified principal — developer, user, or society. Its failure mode, misalignment, is the central object of most technical AI-safety research.
definition_zh: 使人工智能系统按照指定对象——开发者、用户或整个社会——的意图、价值观与规范来运用其能力。与之相对的失败情形（错对齐）是绝大多数技术性人工智能安全研究的核心问题。
pitfalls: 对齐 is fully established but is a dead metaphor in the wrong direction: in ordinary Chinese it is what you do to text in a word processor or parts on an assembly line, so a lay reader hears a mechanical/typographic operation rather than a relationship between an agent's goals and human values. Second and more consequential: the PRC policy register overwhelmingly writes 价值对齐 or 价值观对齐 ('value alignment'), which narrows the concept to values and quietly drops intent-following, controllability and the whole inner/outer alignment apparatus. The TC260 framework's only uses of 对齐 are 价值观、伦理观对齐 and 对齐算法. A translator who renders technical 'alignment' as 价值对齐 in a policy document is making a substantive scope reduction, not a stylistic choice. Third, note the antonym: the official Chinese International AI Safety Report uses 错对齐 for 'misalignment' (not 未对齐 or 失准), which is worth following for consistency.

translations.notes: The bare technical term, standard in research writing and in the official report glossary. Antonym: 错对齐 (misalignment).

attestations.quote_zh: 对齐（Alignment）：人工智能模型或系统倾向于按照人类意图、价值观或规范运用其能力的能力。根据具体语境，此处所指可涉及各类主体的意图与价值取向，例如开发者、用户、特定社群乃至整个社会。
attestations.quote_en: Alignment: the tendency of an AI model or system to apply its capabilities in accordance with human intentions, values or norms. Depending on context this may refer to the intentions and values of various parties, such as developers, users, particular communities, or society as a whole.
attestations.source_title: 《2026 年国际人工智能安全报告》（中文版）词汇表
attestations.publisher: International AI Safety Report（主席 Yoshua Bengio）

attestations.quote_zh: 对于能够在更高级的通用人工智能超越人类智能水平后，仍可靠地确保其对齐，并保持人类的有效控制。
attestations.quote_en: …to reliably ensure alignment and maintain effective human control even after more advanced AGI surpasses human intelligence.
attestations.source_title: “上海共识”（人工智能安全国际对话）报道
attestations.publisher: 澎湃新闻

translations.notes: The full form, used as the Chinese Wikipedia headword and by 智源社区/知乎 explainers. Use when 对齐 alone would be ambiguous.

attestations.quote_zh: 人工智能对齐（英語：AI alignment，或譯為人工智慧校準）是指引导人工智能系统的行为，使其符合设计者的利益和预期目标。
attestations.quote_en: AI alignment (English: AI alignment; also translated 人工智慧校準) means steering the behaviour of AI systems so that it accords with the interests and intended goals of their designers.
attestations.source_title: 人工智能对齐
attestations.publisher: 维基百科（中文）

translations.notes: The PRC policy register's preferred form (also 价值对齐). Narrower than English 'alignment' — covers values and ethics but not intent-following or controllability. Use deliberately, not as a default translation of 'alignment'. No attestation of the contiguous string 价值观对齐 was located in this pass: TC260 1.0, previously cited here, writes the coordinate construction 价值观、伦理观对齐, which is not the same term.

Taiwan/traditional-character variant recorded by Chinese Wikipedia as an alternative title. 校準 (calibration) is arguably a better metaphor than 對齊 but is not used in mainland writing; do not use in PRC-facing text, where 校准 means instrument calibration.

used_by.note: glossary defines both alignment and misalignment

used_by.note: policy register; also 对齐算法

usage_examples.zh: 如果人工智能系统“错对齐”（即其目标与开发者、用户或整个社会的意图相冲突），发生失控的概率就会增大。
usage_examples.en: If an AI system is misaligned — that is, its goals conflict with the intentions of developers, users or society — the probability of loss of control increases.

definition_en: The Redwood Research agenda: designing deployment protocols (trusted monitoring, untrusted monitoring, resampling, auditing) that keep you safe even if the model is actively misaligned and deliberately trying to subvert your safeguards. Control is explicitly the complement of alignment — it assumes the model may already want to defect and asks whether it can succeed.
definition_zh: Redwood Research 提出的研究议程：设计一套部署协议（可信监控、不可信监控、重采样、审计等），使得即便模型已经失准、并且在有意规避安全措施，你依然是安全的。控制与对齐互补——对齐问「模型想不想搞破坏」，控制问「就算它想，能不能得逞」。
pitfalls: THIS IS THE HEADLINE PROBLEM IN THIS CATEGORY. Bare 控制 and 管控 in Chinese AI discourse mean administrative or regulatory control of AI by the state or by developers — the register of 「确保人工智能始终处于人类控制之下」 (Global AI Governance Initiative) and 「安全、可信、可控」 (TC260). Redwood's 'control' means something almost orthogonal: a technical, adversarial, deployment-time discipline that explicitly grants the premise that the model is misaligned. A Chinese reader meeting 人工智能控制 with no gloss will read policy-controllability (可控性), i.e. the very thing the control agenda assumes you have already lost. The distinction that must be preserved is the 'despite' — safety DESPITE misalignment, not safety BY achieving alignment. CSET's official Chinese translation solves this with an explicit contrast sentence rather than with a coined term, which is currently the best practice available: state the alignment/control contrast in full the first time. Do not use 管控 (which adds a supervisory-authority flavour) and do not use 可控性 (controllability, a property, not a research programme).

translations.notes: Used in CSET's own Chinese translation of its explainer, which is a genuine attested EN↔ZH pair (English original 'AI Control: How to Make Use of Misbehaving AI Agents'). The source itself flags the term as new: 「人工智能控制」是一个相对较新的术语. In running Chinese ML text the code-switched AI 控制 is at least as common.

attestations.quote_zh: 人工智能对齐旨在确保人工智能体从一开始就不会试图违规，而人工智能控制旨在确保即使人工智能体追求不当目标，也无法成功达成。
attestations.quote_en: AI alignment aims to ensure AI agents never attempt to misbehave in the first place, whereas AI control aims to ensure that even if AI agents pursue improper goals, they cannot succeed.
attestations.source_title: 人工智能控制：如何利用违规人工智能体
attestations.publisher: Center for Security and Emerging Technology (CSET), Georgetown University；作者 Kendrea Beers, Cody Rushing

translations.notes: Code-switched form typical of Chinese ML writing. Same ambiguity problem as 人工智能控制 — needs a gloss on first use.

translations.zh: 失准前提下的安全保障
translations.pinyin: shīzhǔn qiántí xià de ānquán bǎozhàng
translations.literal_back: safety assurance under the premise of misalignment
translations.notes: We propose this as an explanatory apposition, not a replacement headword: write 人工智能控制（失准前提下的安全保障）on first use. It is unattested — coined here — but it is the only formulation we found that carries the load-bearing 'despite' which every existing Chinese rendering drops. Do not use it as a bare term; a Chinese reader will not recognise it.

Widely used in PRC policy text (TC260 framework, RICE principles in the PKU alignment survey) but it names a desired PROPERTY of a system, not Redwood's research programme. Using it for 'AI control' collapses exactly the distinction the term exists to make. Attested in that other sense: the PKU CCL 2024 survey lists 可控性(Controllability) as one of the four RICE goals.

attestations.quote_zh: 可控性是一种必要的属性，它确保系统的行动和决策过程始终受到人类监督和约束。
attestations.quote_en: Controllability is a necessary property ensuring that a system's actions and decision processes remain under human oversight and constraint.
attestations.source_title: 《对齐的理论、技术与评估》
attestations.publisher: 北京大学人工智能安全与治理中心 / CCL 2024

used_by.note: in the Chinese edition of their AI control explainer; also coins 可信模型 / 不可信模型 / 可信监控 / 不可信监控

usage_examples.zh: 「不可信模型」的定义为功能更强但可能具有蓄意破坏性的新型智能体。
usage_examples.en: An 'untrusted model' is defined as a newer, more capable agent that may be deliberately subversive.

usage_examples.zh: 控制类措施的出发点是：先假设模型已经失准，再问它能不能绕过我们的监控。
usage_examples.en: Control measures start by assuming the model is already misaligned, then ask whether it can get around our monitoring.

definition_en: The normative study of how AI systems should be built and used — fairness, bias, privacy, accountability, human dignity. In most institutions it predates and sits alongside AI safety rather than inside it.
definition_zh: 研究人工智能应当如何被开发和使用的规范性领域，涉及公平、偏见、隐私、问责与人的尊严等议题。在多数机构中，它的建制早于人工智能安全，并与之并列而非从属。
pitfalls: The term itself is stable; the trap is institutional. In PRC discourse 人工智能伦理 is long-established — 《新一代人工智能伦理规范》 dates from 2021, well before the safety framing arrived — and it comes with its own machinery (伦理审查, 科技伦理委员会). Consequently the TC260 framework treats ethics as one risk domain *inside* AI safety (伦理域安全风险), which is close to the inverse of the Anglophone arrangement where 'AI ethics' and 'AI safety' are often rival umbrella framings with different communities. When translating, do not assume 伦理 and 安全 stand in the same relation on both sides. Note too the striking construction 伦理安全 ('ethical safety/security'), which has no natural English equivalent.

translations.notes: Standard and long-established. Also appears in institutional names — 人工智能伦理委员会 (AI ethics committee/board) is the standard rendering used in the official report's discussion of corporate governance.

attestations.quote_zh: 监督与咨询委员会、信托机构或人工智能伦理委员会也可作为风险管理指导与组织监督的机制
attestations.quote_en: Oversight and advisory boards, trusts, or AI ethics committees can also serve as mechanisms for risk-management guidance and organisational oversight.
attestations.source_title: 《2026 年国际人工智能安全报告》（中文版）
attestations.publisher: International AI Safety Report（主席 Yoshua Bengio）

translations.notes: TC260's category, placing ethics as one of four application-risk domains inside AI safety. Recorded because it shows the PRC framework's containment relation between the two fields, which differs from Anglophone usage.

attestations.quote_zh: 3.2.4 伦理域安全风险（a）加剧社会歧视偏见、扩大智能鸿沟的风险。
attestations.quote_en: 3.2.4 Ethics-domain safety risks. (a) The risk of exacerbating social discrimination and bias and widening the intelligence divide.

usage_examples.en: Developers should assess potential bias in model algorithms, strengthen spot-checks on training-data content and quality, and design effective and reliable alignment algorithms to keep values risks and ethical risks controllable.

definition_en: A principle from the 2023 Global AI Governance Initiative: AI development should be oriented toward the good, conform to international law, and accord with the common values of humanity. The 2025 AI+ Opinions go further and call for building a 理论体系 — a theoretical system — of 智能向善, which treats it as a research programme rather than a slogan.
definition_zh: 《全球人工智能治理倡议》（2023）提出的宗旨：发展人工智能应坚持“智能向善”，遵守适用的国际法，符合全人类共同价值。2025年《关于深入实施“人工智能+”行动的意见》进一步要求“探索形成智能向善理论体系”，将其作为研究课题而非口号。
pitfalls: 向善 is a moral-cultivation phrase — 'to turn toward the good' — with roots in the Mencian vocabulary of a subject's inner orientation. It attributes a moral direction to the development of the technology itself. English 'AI for good' is instrumental: AI deployed in service of good ends, a usage associated with humanitarian applications and UN-branded programmes. The Chinese is a stronger and more moralised claim, and it is stated as a 宗旨, a founding purpose, not an application area. The gap matters when reading PRC positions in international fora: an English reader sees a familiar and rather thin slogan where the Chinese text is asserting a normative orientation for the whole enterprise.

en_renderings.notes: This IS the official English — the PRC's own translation of the Global AI Governance Initiative renders 坚持“智能向善”的宗旨 as 'adhere to the principle of developing AI for good'. It is therefore the attested rendering even though it is weaker than the Chinese. CSET independently uses the same phrase for the 2025 AI+ Opinions.

attestations.quote_zh: ——发展人工智能应坚持“智能向善”的宗旨，遵守适用的国际法，符合和平、发展、公平、正义、民主、自由的全人类共同价值，共同防范和打击恐怖主义、极端势力和跨国有组织犯罪集团对人工智能技术的恶用滥用。
attestations.quote_en: We must adhere to the principle of developing AI for good, respect the relevant international laws, and align AI development with humanity's common values of peace, development, equity, justice, democracy, and freedom. We should work together to prevent and fight against the misuse and malicious use of AI technologies by terrorists, extreme forces, and transnational organized criminal groups.
attestations.source_title: 《全球人工智能治理倡议》 / Global AI Governance Initiative
attestations.publisher: 国家互联网信息办公室 (CAC); official English via Embassy of the PRC in the USA

attestations.quote_zh: 深入研究人工智能对人类认知判断、伦理规范等方面的深层次影响和作用机理，探索形成智能向善理论体系，促进人工智能更好造福人类。
attestations.quote_en: Conduct in-depth research on AI's profound impacts and mechanisms of action on human cognitive judgments and ethical norms, and explore development of a theoretical system of 'AI for good' (智能向善), to encourage technology that better benefits humanity.
attestations.source_title: 国务院关于深入实施“人工智能+”行动的意见 / Opinions of the State Council on Deepening the Implementation of the "Artificial Intelligence+" Initiative
attestations.publisher: 国务院 (State Council); English translation by CSET, Georgetown University

en_renderings.notes: We advocate this, or 'AI turned toward the good', where the reader needs to see that the Chinese makes a claim about the moral direction of the technology rather than about beneficial applications. Not attested; the official English is 'AI for good' and should be cited as such.

why_no_english: English has 'AI for good' as a fixed collocation with a settled, instrumental meaning, so the strong reading is unavailable — the phrase is already occupied. And English has no equivalent of 向善 as a compact verb of moral orientation applied to a non-person: 'tending toward the good' is philosophical and archaic, 'beneficial' is an outcome, 'ethical' is a constraint. The Chinese term does something English can only do at sentence length.

used_by.note: a named 宗旨 in the Global AI Governance Initiative; official English 'developing AI for good'
2025 AI+ Opinions call for a theoretical system of it

usage_examples.en: The development of AI should uphold the purpose of AI for good.

definition_en: The institutions, norms, laws and processes by which societies steer AI development and deployment — spanning company policy, national regulation and international agreements.
definition_zh: 指社会引导人工智能研发与部署所依托的制度、规范、法律与流程，涵盖企业内部政策、国家监管与国际协议等层面。
pitfalls: 治理 is correct and established, but the three near-synonyms carry different political weight and are not interchangeable. 治理 (governance) implies multi-stakeholder, multi-level steering including self-regulation and international coordination, and is the word PRC documents use for the outward-facing, cooperative frame (《全球人工智能治理倡议》). 监管 (regulation/supervision) names state enforcement by an agency and is narrower and harder-edged. 管理 (management/administration) is the word of administrative measures over a licensed activity — note that China's generative-AI rules are 《生成式人工智能服务管理暂行办法》, using 管理, not 治理, precisely because they are binding administrative rules. Rendering all three as 'governance' in English flattens a real distinction about who is doing what to whom; rendering English 'governance' as 监管 in a Chinese document narrows a cooperative frame into a regulatory one and can change the political reading of a text.

translations.notes: The standard term across PRC policy, international documents and academia. Appears in the title of China's 《全球人工智能治理倡议》 and in the TC260 framework.

attestations.quote_en: Promote international cooperation on AI safety governance worldwide, share best practices, advocate open platforms, and through cross-disciplinary, cross-sector, cross-regional and cross-border dialogue and cooperation, work toward a global AI governance system with broad consensus.

translations.notes: Use for English 'regulation' specifically — state enforcement by a competent authority. Narrower and more coercive than 治理; not a stylistic variant of it. No attestation of the contiguous compound 人工智能监管 was located in this pass: the Chinese International AI Safety Report, previously cited here, uses 监管 only in other compounds (监管体系, 监管机构) and contains zero occurrences of 人工智能监管.
The administrative-measures register. China's binding generative-AI rules are 《生成式人工智能服务管理暂行办法》 — 管理, not 治理. Do not use for English 'governance'.
A named principle in Chinese AI policy, not merely a description. Recorded because it is a Chinese-side term of art an EN→ZH translator will meet and should not paraphrase away.

definition_en: The State Council initiative, formalised in the August 2025 Opinions, for driving AI into every sector of the economy and society — S&T, industry, consumption, livelihoods, governance and global cooperation. Modelled on 互联网+ (Internet Plus, 2015). Its existence signals a diffusion-first rather than frontier-first national strategy: the document is about adoption across 千行百业, not about building the most capable model.
definition_zh: 2025年8月国务院《关于深入实施“人工智能+”行动的意见》确立的国家行动，推动人工智能与科技、产业、消费、民生、治理、全球合作等各领域深度融合，仿照2015年的“互联网+”。其重心是全行业扩散应用，而非前沿模型能力竞赛。
pitfalls: The '+' is a productive policy morpheme in Chinese, inherited from 互联网+, meaning roughly 'apply X across every sector as a national campaign'. English has no such suffix, so renderings either keep the plus sign (opaque) or paraphrase it as 'AI adoption' / 'AI diffusion' (loses the campaign character, the sectoral checklist and the implied central mobilisation). Note also that 人工智能+ is older than the 2025 initiative in a different sense: the 2017 AI Development Plan already used 「人工智能+X」 for interdisciplinary university degree programmes. Do not read every occurrence as a reference to the State Council initiative.

en_renderings.notes: The rendering an English reader will meet in coverage; parallels the established 'Internet Plus'. Keeps the morpheme at the cost of explaining nothing.

attestations.quote_zh: 全面实施“人工智能+”行动，以人工智能引领科研范式变革，加强人工智能同产业发展、文化建设、民生保障、社会治理相结合，抢占人工智能产业应用制高点，全方位赋能千行百业。

why_no_english: English policy has no compositional suffix that turns a technology name into the name of a national diffusion campaign. 'X+' does exactly that in PRC usage and is immediately legible to a Chinese reader as 'the Internet Plus treatment, applied to X': a State Council opinion, a sectoral enumeration, provincial implementation plans and a target date. Rendering it as 'AI adoption' describes the outcome and deletes the apparatus.

definition_en: The field concerned with preventing AI systems from causing harm — whether through accident, malfunction, misuse or loss of control — and with the techniques and institutions that make advanced AI reliably beneficial.
definition_zh: 研究如何防止人工智能系统造成危害的领域，涵盖事故、故障、滥用与失控等各类成因，也包括为使先进人工智能可靠有益而发展的技术手段与制度安排。
pitfalls: This is the headline translation problem of the whole field. Chinese 安全 covers English safety, security AND (in 国家安全) national security, and the default rendering 人工智能安全 therefore silently collapses distinctions that the English discourse treats as load-bearing. Three specific hazards. (1) Institutional mismatch: 《人工智能安全治理框架》 is issued by the 全国网络安全标准化技术委员会 — the *cybersecurity* standards committee — yet is officially titled 'AI Safety Governance Framework' in English. The same character string 安全 does both jobs in a single document. (2) Direction of drift: because 安全 in PRC institutional usage is anchored to 网络安全/信息安全/国家安全, a Chinese reader encountering 人工智能安全 defaults to the security reading, i.e. protecting systems and the state *from* attack, not protecting the world from the model. English 'AI safety' advocacy read through 人工智能安全 therefore lands as a cybersecurity/content-control agenda. (3) There is an emerging fix but it is neither general nor, within its own source, complete: the official Chinese edition of the 2026 International AI Safety Report glosses 安全（Safety） and 安保（Security） as separate glossary entries and uses 安保 in security contexts, but applies the split only partially (25 occurrences of 安保 vs 465 of 安全; 网络安全 left unconverted). A 2026 arXiv terminological proposal (arXiv:2605.13069, verified) argues for making the split general across Chinese CS and engineering. See the ai-security entry. When precision matters, write 人工智能安全（safety） or adopt the 安全/安保 split explicitly; do not assume context will carry the distinction.

translations.notes: The universal default across policy, industry and research. Ambiguous between safety and security by construction; the ambiguity is a property of the term, not of any particular author's sloppiness. The TC260 framework uses it 57 times in 16 pages, spanning model-algorithm risk, data security, cyberattack, content control and ethics — the full safety∪security range under one word.

definition_en: TC260's non-binding technical document setting out China's AI risk taxonomy and countermeasures. Version 1.0 was released 9 September 2024; version 2.0 on 15 September 2025, adding a three-way risk taxonomy (technology-inherent, technology-application, application-derived) and a five-level risk grading scale.
definition_zh: 全国网络安全标准化技术委员会发布的技术文件，系统提出中国的人工智能安全风险分类与应对措施。1.0 版于 2024 年 9 月 9 日发布，2.0 版于 2025 年 9 月 15 日发布，新增技术内生、技术应用、应用衍生三类风险划分，并探索五级风险分级。
pitfalls: Chinese-origin document — cite the Chinese. The 2.0 PDF is bilingual on its title page and gives its own English title as 'AI Safety Governance Framework 2.0', so 安全 here is officially rendered *safety*; be aware that secondary English commentary sometimes renders it 'AI Security Governance Framework', and the document's contents in fact cover security (漏洞, 后门, 供应链) as much as safety. It is a 技术文件, not a 国家标准 — it is not mandatory and carries no penalties, so calling it 'China's AI safety standard' overstates it. Note also that 治理 (governance) not 监管 (regulation) is in the title, consistent with its non-binding status.

translations.notes: Official title. The document's own title page carries the English 'AI Safety Governance Framework 2.0', making this one of the strongest attested EN↔ZH pairs in the whole category.

attestations.quote_zh: 为应对人工智能快速发展的新风险新挑战，安全有效地释放应用需求，促进人工智能技术和产业发展，在国家互联网信息办公室的指导下，全国网络安全标准化技术委员会组织国家计算机网络应急技术处理协调中心等专业机构、科研院所、行业企业，持续跟踪风险变化，梳理调整风险分类，研究探索风险分级方法，动态调整更新防范治理措施，制定《人工智能安全治理框架》2.0 版。

en_aliases: Center for AI Standards and Innovation
definition_en: A government-backed body that evaluates frontier AI models and develops safety testing methodology. The UK and US created the first two in 2023; an International Network of AI Safety Institutes was launched at the 2024 Seoul summit. The US body was reorganised as the Center for AI Standards and Innovation (CAISI) in June 2025.
definition_zh: 由政府设立或支持、负责评测前沿人工智能模型并研究安全测试方法的专门机构。英国和美国于 2023 年率先设立，2024 年首尔峰会上成立了人工智能安全研究所国际网络。中国没有对应的监管型机构，而是在 2025 年 2 月成立了以对外交流为主的「中国人工智能发展与安全研究网络」。
pitfalls: The Chinese term is a straightforward calque, but the institutional referent does not exist in the PRC. China's nearest counterpart, 中国人工智能发展与安全研究网络 (CnAISDA, launched around the February 2025 Paris summit), is a 网络 (network) of existing institutes, not a 研究所, and does not test frontier models or hold regulatory power — so 'China's AI Safety Institute' is a misleading gloss. Note also that IDAIS's own Chinese text renders 'AI safety authorities' as 安全监管部门 (safety *regulatory* departments), a different institutional idea from a research institute. Finally, the US renaming to CAISI dropped 安全 entirely: 美国人工智能标准与创新中心 has no 安全 in it, and Chinese sources mark this by writing （原人工智能安全研究所）.

translations.notes: Standard rendering for the UK/US/Japan/Korea bodies and for the international network. Used unchanged by CAICT, 安全内参 and Chinese media.

definition_en: Anthropic's tiered scheme, modelled on biosafety levels, in which each level pairs a description of model capability with the security and deployment safeguards required at that level. ASL-3 was first triggered in 2025.
definition_zh: Anthropic参照生物安全等级（BSL）设计的分级体系，每一级都把模型能力的描述与该级别必须落实的安保与部署防护措施配对。ASL-3于2025年首次被触发。
pitfalls: The collision the hint flags is real and worth stating carefully. PRC cybersecurity has a legally mandated, deeply entrenched grading regime — 网络安全等级保护 ('MLPS', colloquially 等保), with five levels, its own national standards (e.g. GB/T 25070-2019) and a compliance step literally called 等级测评. The Shanghai AI Lab / Concordia AI frontier framework cites 等级保护 in its security section, so both vocabularies genuinely coexist in one Chinese AI-safety document. A bare 安全等级 in PRC context will therefore be read as an MLPS compliance grade — a static grading of the system's protection level assigned by regulation — not as a capability-triggered tier that a model can cross during training. Keep the AI/ASL prefix (AI安全等级(ASL)) rather than writing 安全等级 alone. Secondary point: 安全 here means safety, whereas in 等级保护 it means security; the collapse makes the two look even more alike than they are.

translations.notes: Concordia AI's form; normally written with (ASL) appended.

definition_en: Protecting AI systems and their assets — weights, training data, code, infrastructure — against deliberate adversarial interference: cyberattack, model theft, tampering, insider threat. Distinguished from safety by the presence of an adversary.
definition_zh: 指保护人工智能系统及其权重、训练数据、代码和基础设施等资产，使其免遭蓄意对抗性干扰，包括网络攻击、模型窃取、篡改和内部威胁。与 safety 的区别在于是否存在有意的攻击者。
pitfalls: The default rendering is also 人工智能安全, identical to AI safety, so by default the distinction simply does not survive translation. Two escape routes exist and both have costs. (1) Sub-domain words: 网络安全 (cybersecurity), 信息安全 (information security), 数据安全 (data security), 模型权重安全 (weights security) are all stable and unambiguous — but they are hyponyms; there is no established Chinese superordinate for 'security' as such, which is precisely the gap the 2026 arXiv proposal identifies. (2) 安保: the official Chinese edition of the 2026 International AI Safety Report gives 安保（Security） its own glossary entry alongside 安全（Safety） and uses 安保 in security contexts — but the split is partial, not systematic: 25 occurrences of 安保 against 465 of 安全, with 网络安全 (25 occurrences) left unconverted. Zhao's 2026 arXiv proposal (arXiv:2605.13069, verified) argues for standardising on 安保/安保性 generally; 安保性 itself does not occur in the report. The cost is register: in everyday Mandarin 安保 most often means physical security or security guards (安保人员), so 人工智能安保 can read oddly to a general audience even though it is now attested in a flagship international document. Also note that 安全 in PRC institutional language is additionally entangled with 国家安全 (national security), a legally defined term — a third sense the English pair does not have at all.

translations.notes: The disambiguating choice, but note how narrow the evidence for the full compound is: 人工智能安保 as a unit is attested only in the bilingual glossary of Zhao (2026, arXiv:2605.13069), which is proposing it. The official Chinese International AI Safety Report supports the underlying 安全/安保 split (see the 安保 entry below) but never writes 人工智能安保 itself. Not used in PRC-native writing.

Verified counts in that PDF: 25 occurrences of 安保 against 465 of 安全, with 网络安全 (25 occurrences) left unconverted — so the split is glossed and partially applied, not applied throughout. 安保性 does not occur in the report at all; it comes from Zhao (2026), who proposes generalising the split across Chinese CS and engineering.

definition_en: A scenario in which AI systems acquire decisive control over the resources and institutions that determine humanity's future, whether by seizing them or by being handed them.
definition_zh: 指AI系统取得对决定人类未来的资源和机构的决定性控制权，无论这种控制是被夺取的还是被交出去的。
pitfalls: Register is the problem, not vocabulary. 接管 is a perfectly ordinary word (a bank being taken over by regulators, a shift being handed over) and 'AI 接管' is transparent — but in Chinese it reads as film-poster language, and Chinese technical and policy writing avoids it almost entirely, preferring 失控 for anything in this neighbourhood. 夺权 is worse: it is squarely political-coup vocabulary in PRC register. No attestation of AI 接管 as a technical term was recovered in this pass; Chinese Wikipedia has no article at 人工智能接管. Practical recommendation: in serious Chinese prose, use 失控 with an explicit definition rather than 接管.

translations.notes: Transparent calque, but no citable Chinese technical or policy use was located. Reads as science-fiction register. Offered only where the English term must be rendered directly.
Recommend against. In PRC Chinese 夺权 denotes a political coup and carries heavy historical baggage; applying it to a model is both sensational and politically distracting.

usage_examples.zh: 中文文献很少直接说“AI 接管”，通常用“失控”并加以定义。
usage_examples.en: Chinese sources rarely say 'AI takeover' outright; they normally use 'loss of control' and define it.

definition_en: The mandatory notification regime created by the 2022 Provisions on the Management of Algorithmic Recommendations in Internet Information Services. A provider whose algorithmic recommendation service has "public opinion attributes or social mobilisation capability" must, within 10 working days of *beginning* to provide the service, submit prescribed particulars — provider name, service form, application domain, algorithm type, an algorithm self-assessment report and the text it intends to publish — through the Internet Information Service Algorithm Filing System, and is then issued a filing number that must be displayed on the service. The regulator grants filing when the materials are complete and refuses it when they are not; it does not licence, approve or vet the algorithm on the merits, and filing happens after launch rather than before it.
definition_zh: 《互联网信息服务算法推荐管理规定》确立的强制性告知制度。具有舆论属性或者社会动员能力的算法推荐服务提供者，应当在提供服务之日起十个工作日内，通过互联网信息服务算法备案系统填报名称、服务形式、应用领域、算法类型、算法自评估报告、拟公示内容等信息，履行备案手续，取得备案编号并公示。网信部门对材料齐全者予以备案，材料不齐全者不予备案；备案本身不是行政许可，不构成对算法的实质性批准。
pitfalls: The single most damaging error in English coverage is calling 备案 'approval', 'licensing' or 'permitting'. 备案 is a completed-formality notification: the regulator's only stated ground for refusing is that materials are incomplete (第二十五条), and the duty attaches ten working days *after* service launch, not before it. Chinese administrative law distinguishes 备案 (record-filing) sharply from 许可 (licensing/permission) and from 核准 (ratification); English regulatory vocabulary collapses all three under 'registration'/'approval'. Rendering it as approval makes the regime sound like a pre-market gate it is not, and simultaneously understates it, because the real leverage lies elsewhere — in the 安全评估 duty (第二十七条), in the self-assessment report the filing must contain, and in the fact that a filing number can be publicly withheld. Note also the asymmetry with 生成式人工智能服务备案, where in practice the pre-launch security assessment does function as a gate. 'Registration' is a defensible second choice but suggests a register of entitlements; 'filing' is closer.

en_renderings.notes: The rendering an English reader will actually meet: used consistently by DigiChina/Stanford, China Law Translate and CSET for 备案 across all the CAC instruments. 'Filing formalities' for 备案手续 and 'algorithm filing system' for 算法备案系统 are the settled forms. Recommended.

attestations.quote_zh: 具有舆论属性或者社会动员能力的算法推荐服务提供者应当在提供服务之日起十个工作日内通过互联网信息服务算法备案系统填报服务提供者的名称、服务形式、应用领域、算法类型、算法自评估报告、拟公示内容等信息，履行备案手续。
attestations.quote_en: Providers of algorithmic recommendation services with public opinion properties or having social mobilization capabilities shall, within 10 working days of providing services, report the provider's name, form of service, domain of application, algorithm type, algorithm self-assessment report, content intended to be publicized, and other such information through the Internet information service algorithm filing system, and carry out filing formalities.
attestations.source_title: 《互联网信息服务算法推荐管理规定》第二十四条
attestations.publisher: 国家互联网信息办公室 等四部门 (Cyberspace Administration of China et al.)

attestations.quote_zh: 国家和省、自治区、直辖市网信部门收到备案人提交的备案材料后，材料齐全的，应当在三十个工作日内予以备案，发放备案编号并进行公示；材料不齐全的，不予备案，并应当在三十个工作日内通知备案人并说明理由。
attestations.quote_en: The national and provincial, autonomous region, and municipal cybersecurity and informatization departments shall, after receiving filing materials submitted by a filing applicant, and where the materials are complete, grant filing within 30 working days, and issue a filing number and publish the matter; where materials are not complete, filing is not to be granted, and the filing applicant shall be notified within 30 working days, and the reason explained.
attestations.source_title: Translation: Internet Information Service Algorithmic Recommendation Management Provisions (Article 25)
attestations.publisher: DigiChina, Stanford University (trans. Rogier Creemers, Graham Webster, Helen Toner)

en_renderings.notes: Used as a shorthand for the system as a whole (the public database of filed algorithms) rather than for the act of filing. Concordia AI glosses it explicitly as a filing system, which is the right pairing. Useful in English prose; do not let it imply that entry on the register confers rights.

attestations.quote_en: The regulation illustrates how China's algorithm registry (the mandatory filing system for all public-facing AI services) can be extended with domain-specific requirements.
attestations.source_title: State of AI Safety in China (2026)
attestations.publisher: Concordia AI (安远 AI)

why_no_english: English regulatory vocabulary has 'registration' (which creates or records a legal status), 'licensing' (which grants permission) and 'notification' (which is often voluntary or purely informational), but nothing for what 备案 is: a legally compulsory, post-hoc, publicly numbered notification whose refusal turns solely on completeness of paperwork and which confers no approval whatsoever, yet which is the hook on which every downstream duty — self-assessment, security assessment, inspection, log retention, rectification orders — is hung. The whole PRC administrative-law contrast between 备案 and 行政许可 is invisible in English, so translators must either use 'filing' (accurate but weak-sounding, which understates the regime's practical bite) or 'approval' (which is legally false). Neither word carries the two-part structure — trivial to obtain, enormously consequential to have — that makes 备案 a workable governance instrument.

used_by.note: 'filing formalities' / 'algorithm filing system' throughout their translation of the 2022 Provisions
'perform formalities for the filing, modification, or canceling of filings on algorithms' in the Generative AI Interim Measures, Art. 17
'China's algorithm registry (the mandatory filing system for all public-facing AI services)'
