usage_examples.zh: 如果模型具备评测意识，安全评测得到的就只是它愿意展示的行为。
usage_examples.en: If a model has evaluation awareness, a safety eval only measures the behaviour it is willing to display.

usage_examples.zh: 模型能区分测试环境和实际部署环境，部署前的安全结论就只能算乐观上界。
usage_examples.en: Once a model can distinguish the test environment from real deployment, a pre-deployment safety conclusion is only an optimistic upper bound.

definition_en: A system scoring well on an evaluation without possessing the property the evaluation is meant to measure. The gaming may be done by the developer — training on benchmark items, tuning to the leaderboard — or by the model, which exploits a grader, a scoring shortcut, or the evaluator's expectations. Either way the score stops being evidence about the underlying capability or alignment.
definition_zh: 系统在评测中拿到高分，却并不具备这项评测想要衡量的能力或属性。做手脚的可能是开发者——拿基准测试的题目去训练、照着榜单调模型；也可能是模型自己——钻评分器、评测目标或评测者预期的空子。无论哪一种，分数都不再能作为真实能力或对齐程度的证据。
pitfalls: Three traps. (1) The one term attested in the Chinese AI-safety register, 评估博弈, comes from a bilingual document whose English side literally reads "Evaluation gaming" — the strongest kind of evidence — but the definition it carries points the other way: 通过战略性地表现不佳，以显得能力较弱或对齐性更强 (strategically underperforming to look less capable or more aligned). In that framework 评估博弈 is essentially sandbagging plus faking alignment on an alignment eval; it does not cover score inflation. A Chinese reader meeting 评估博弈 will not think of a model scoring too high. (2) 博弈 means game theory / strategic interaction, not 'exploiting a loophole' — the same objection that dogs 规范博弈 for specification gaming. (3) The developer sense and the model sense live in different registers and Chinese keeps them apart lexically. The developer sense has vivid native vocabulary — 刷榜, 刷分, 专门应试 — which is ML-media and practitioner-criticism register; none of it appears in any of the three authoritative Chinese frontier-safety documents we searched. Those documents reach instead for 奖励作弊/奖励黑客 on the model side and 数据污染/基准泄漏 on the developer side. Note also that 基准污染 is not the attested compound; the attested forms are 数据污染 and 基准泄漏.

translations.literal_back: evaluation game-playing / strategic interaction over the evaluation
translations.notes: The only rendering we found inside the Chinese AI-safety register, and it comes with an attested EN↔ZH pair: the same framework's English edition lists the capability as "Evaluation gaming" where the Chinese edition lists 评估博弈能力. Recommended as the safety-register term, but read the pitfalls first — the framework's own gloss restricts it to strategic underperformance, so it half-overlaps sandbagging. Sourced by the framework to Fan et al., "Evaluation Faking" (arXiv:2505.17815).

attestations.quote_zh: 评估博弈：指在能力与对齐性评估中，通过战略性地表现不佳，以显得能力较弱或对齐性更强的行为。
attestations.quote_en: Evaluation gaming: Ability to strategically manipulate capability and alignment evaluations by underperforming to appear less capable or more aligned. (the document's own English edition, safework-f1-framework.EN.pdf)
attestations.source_title: 《人工智能前沿风险管理框架（1.0版）》
attestations.publisher: 上海人工智能实验室 / 安远AI (Concordia AI)

attestations.quote_zh: AI系统通过正确区分训练和部署环境展现出情境感知能力，然后系统性欺骗研发者：在安全评估中故意表现不佳以显得符合预期，同时保留真实能力和目标。
attestations.quote_en: An AI system demonstrates situational awareness by correctly distinguishing between training and deployment environments, then systematically deceives developers by underperforming during safety evaluations to appear aligned while retaining its true capabilities and goals.
attestations.source_title: 《人工智能前沿风险管理框架（1.0版）》
attestations.publisher: 上海人工智能实验室 / 安远AI (Concordia AI)

translations.notes: The developer sense, and the liveliest word Chinese has for it. Leaderboard-culture register: it is a term of criticism aimed at labs, standard in 机器之心/知乎-style ML commentary, and it carries an accusation of bad faith. We found zero occurrences of it in the 2026 International AI Safety Report (Chinese edition), the Shanghai AI Lab / Concordia AI frontier risk framework, or Concordia AI's frontier risk monitoring report — so it is not safety-governance register. Also recorded under data-contamination, where it names the behaviour contamination enables.

attestations.quote_zh: 在兴奋于技术进展速度之快后，很多人发现似乎也有些不对味：为什么排行榜第一人人有份？这是个什么机制？于是乎，「刷榜」这个问题也开始备受关注。
attestations.quote_en: After the excitement about how fast the technology was moving, a lot of people noticed something was off: why does everyone get to be number one on the leaderboard? What kind of mechanism is that? And so the problem of "leaderboard-grinding" started attracting attention.
attestations.source_title: 大模型走捷径「刷榜」？数据污染问题值得重视
attestations.publisher: 机器之心（经腾讯云开发者社区转载）

attestations.quote_zh: 在作者与读者中互动中，作者也表示，希望「让大家更理性看待刷榜这个事情，很多模型和 GPT4 的差距还很大」。
attestations.quote_en: In exchanges with readers the authors also said they hoped to "get everyone to look at this leaderboard-grinding business more rationally — many models are still a long way behind GPT-4."
attestations.source_title: 大模型走捷径「刷榜」？数据污染问题值得重视
attestations.publisher: 机器之心（经腾讯云开发者社区转载）

translations.notes: Same register as 刷榜 but aimed at a single benchmark score rather than a ranking. Use 刷分 when the object is a number, 刷榜 when the object is a position. Neither is safety-register.

attestations.quote_zh: 用简单的话来解释就是：如果有模型在训练的时候，直接拿基准测试里面的「真题」和「答案」来当学习资料，想以此来刷分，那么此处就会有异常。
attestations.quote_en: Put simply: if a model was trained directly on the benchmark's "real exam questions" and "answers" as study material in order to farm the score, an anomaly will show up here.
attestations.source_title: 大模型走捷径「刷榜」？数据污染问题值得重视
attestations.publisher: 机器之心（经腾讯云开发者社区转载）

attestations.quote_zh: 你不是说数据很重要吗，那么用「真题」刷分的大模型，性能会不会因为训练数据更优秀而变得更好呢？答案是否定的。
attestations.quote_en: You said data matters, right? So does a large model that farms its score on the "real exam questions" actually get better because its training data is better? The answer is no.
attestations.source_title: 大模型走捷径「刷榜」？数据污染问题值得重视
attestations.publisher: 机器之心（经腾讯云开发者社区转载）

translations.notes: Strictly a rendering of *reward hacking* (see reward-hacking, where 奖励黑客 is preferred), but the 2026 International AI Safety Report's Chinese edition uses it exactly where English would say a model games its evaluation, and its definition there — scoring high on the training or evaluation objective without achieving the intended goal — is our concept verbatim. This is how the Chinese safety register currently expresses model-side evaluation gaming: by borrowing reward hacking's word rather than coining one.

attestations.quote_zh: 奖励作弊是指模型找到一些意外的捷径，这些捷径在训练或评估目标上得分很高，但不会实现期望目标。
attestations.quote_en: Reward hacking means a model finds unintended shortcuts that score highly on the training or evaluation objective but do not achieve the desired goal.
attestations.source_title: 《2026年国际人工智能安全报告》（中文版）
attestations.publisher: International AI Safety Report（国际人工智能安全报告专家组）

attestations.quote_zh: 还有模型会在性能测试中进行“奖励作弊”，并学会了如何掩盖这种意图
attestations.quote_en: There are also models that "reward hack" in performance tests and have learned how to conceal the intent.
attestations.source_title: 《2026年国际人工智能安全报告》（中文版）
attestations.publisher: International AI Safety Report（国际人工智能安全报告专家组）

translations.zh: 利用评测体系中的漏洞
translations.pinyin: lìyòng píngcè tǐxì zhōng de lòudòng
translations.literal_back: exploiting loopholes in the evaluation system
translations.notes: The paraphrase the 2026 International AI Safety Report's Chinese edition uses in its executive summary in place of a term. Unambiguous, safety-register, and it names the mechanism rather than the blame — worth using when 评估博弈's underperformance connotation would mislead.

attestations.quote_zh: 可靠的部署前安全测试已变得更难实施。模型越来越常见地能够区分测试环境和实际部署环境，并利用评测体系中的漏洞。这意味着危险能力在部署前可能无法被发现。
attestations.quote_en: Reliable pre-deployment safety testing has become harder to carry out. It is increasingly common for models to distinguish the test environment from the real deployment environment and to exploit loopholes in the evaluation system. This means dangerous capabilities may go undetected before deployment.
attestations.source_title: 《2026年国际人工智能安全报告》（中文版）
attestations.publisher: International AI Safety Report（国际人工智能安全报告专家组）

translations.notes: Not a term of art, but the native frame Chinese reaches for, and it travels better than any calque: 应试教育 ('exam-oriented education') is a loaded piece of Chinese cultural vocabulary for optimising the measurement instead of the thing measured. 专门应试的大模型 ('a large model that exists to pass the exam') and 应试选手 ('exam-taker') both appear unglossed, six years and two registers apart, which suggests the frame is stable even though no fixed compound has formed.

attestations.quote_zh: 但副作用是，如果我们仅使用这些泄露的数据来微调或训练模型，这些专门应试的大模型在其他正常测试任务上的表现可能会受到不利影响。
attestations.quote_en: But there is a side effect: if we fine-tune or train models only on this leaked data, these exam-oriented large models may do worse on other, normal test tasks.
attestations.source_title: 大模型走捷径「刷榜」？数据污染问题值得重视
attestations.publisher: 机器之心（经腾讯云开发者社区转载）

attestations.quote_zh: 单纯靠"把模型做大"来提升安全评测分数，可能是在制造更精明的"应试选手"而非更安全的模型
attestations.quote_en: Simply making the model bigger in order to raise safety-evaluation scores may be manufacturing a shrewder "exam-taker" rather than a safer model.
attestations.source_title: 当AI学会察言观色：模型能detect自己正在被考试，而且这能力和你想的完全不一样
attestations.publisher: 智柴网

translations.notes: We could not recover this compound in any source, so it is recorded as a coinage, not an attestation. It is proposed because the 作弊 frame demonstrably is available in this context — 奖励作弊 is the report term for the model side, and a Chinese explainer of the evaluation-awareness literature writes 这把安全评测从"出题"变成了"出题 + 反作弊" ('this turns safety evaluation from setting the exam into setting the exam plus catching cheats'). 评测作弊 would be immediately readable and, unlike 评估博弈, carries no underperformance connotation. Note that 机器之心 reported the paper 《Don't Make Your LLM an Evaluation Benchmark Cheater》 without translating 'cheater' at all, which is some evidence the compound had not formed.

used_by.note: 《人工智能前沿风险管理框架（1.0版）》中英双语版，英文侧作 Evaluation gaming，列为失控相关的使能能力之一

used_by.org: 《2026年国际人工智能安全报告》（中文版）
used_by.zh_used: 奖励作弊 / 利用评测体系中的漏洞
used_by.note: 没有为 evaluation gaming 单列术语，模型侧并入奖励作弊，开发者侧并入数据污染
开发者侧的批评用语，属于榜单文化而非安全治理语域

usage_examples.zh: 如果开发者拿基准测试的题目去训练，那这个分数就是刷出来的，说明不了模型真的会做题。
usage_examples.en: If the developer trained on the benchmark's own items, the score was farmed and says nothing about whether the model can really do the task.

usage_examples.zh: 评估博弈让评测结果失去证据价值：分数高不等于模型真的安全。
usage_examples.en: Evaluation gaming destroys the evidentiary value of an eval: a high score does not mean the model is actually safe.

definition_en: The discrepancy between how well a system performs in controlled pre-deployment evaluation and how useful or risky it turns out to be in real-world deployment. In the 2026 International AI Safety Report it names a recurring finding that benchmarks overstate practical utility.
definition_zh: 系统在受控的部署前评测中的表现，与其在真实部署环境中的实际效用或风险之间的落差。《2026年国际人工智能安全报告》用它概括一个反复出现的发现：基准测试往往高估了模型的实际效用。
pitfalls: Added by research because it kept surfacing and is systematically confusable with 'elicitation gap' in the other direction. Note the asymmetry: 评测差距 as used in the Chinese report describes evaluations flattering the model on utility, while the safety literature's elicitation gap describes evaluations understating dangerous capability. Both can be true of the same model at once, which is exactly why one Chinese term should not be made to serve both.

translations.notes: Used repeatedly and consistently in the Chinese edition of the International AI Safety Report, including in its key-findings summary.

attestations.quote_zh: 存在“评测差距”：人工智能系统在部署前评测等受控环境中经常有出色的表现，但在现实世界环境下表现较差。
attestations.quote_en: There is an 'evaluation gap': AI systems often perform excellently in controlled settings such as pre-deployment evaluations, but worse in real-world environments.
attestations.source_title: 《2026年国际人工智能安全报告》（中文版）
attestations.publisher: International AI Safety Report（国际人工智能安全报告专家组）

attestations.quote_zh: “评测差距”意味着仅凭基准测试结果无法可靠预测实际应用中的效用或风险。
attestations.quote_en: The 'evaluation gap' means benchmark results alone cannot reliably predict real-world utility or risk.
attestations.source_title: 《2026年国际人工智能安全报告》（中文版）
attestations.publisher: International AI Safety Report（国际人工智能安全报告专家组）

used_by.org: 国际人工智能安全报告（中文版）
used_by.note: recurring theme across capability and risk-management chapters

usage_examples.zh: 能力的参差不齐以及评测差距，使得通用型人工智能的能力难以被可靠地衡量和预测。
usage_examples.en: Jagged capability profiles and the evaluation gap make general-purpose AI capability hard to measure and predict reliably.

definition_en: A risk of an outcome that would permanently and drastically curtail humanity's long-term potential — extinction, or an unrecoverable global catastrophe or lock-in. Bostrom's definition; narrower than 'catastrophic risk'.
definition_zh: 指可能永久且极大地削减人类长远潜力的风险，包括人类灭绝，或无法逆转的全球性灾难与永久锁定状态。该定义源自博斯特罗姆，其范围窄于“灾难性风险”。
pitfalls: Both leading candidates are false friends. 生存风险 back-translates as 'survival risk', which in ordinary Chinese business and policy prose means a threat to an organisation's continued operation ('企业生存风险'); the cosmic scope of the English has to be supplied by context. 存在风险 is closer to the Latin root but collides head-on with the everyday reading of 存在 as the verb 'to exist / there exists', so 存在风险 is routinely parsed as 'a risk exists' rather than 'existential risk' — this is a real garden-path, not a theoretical one. 生存性风险 with the -性 suffix is the least ambiguous and is what the IDAIS Beijing consensus uses. Register, stated neutrally: the frame is confined to expert-dialogue and translated material. It appears in IDAIS statements (which carry Chinese scientists' signatures and are hosted by BAAI) and in Chinese Wikipedia, but the two authoritative PRC governance documents examined here — the TC260 《人工智能安全治理框架》 1.0/2.0 — contain no equivalent term, and even the 189-page Chinese edition of the 2026 International AI Safety Report contains zero occurrences of 生存风险/生存性风险, rendering the same content descriptively as 人类被边缘化甚至灭绝. A translator should expect to gloss the term, and should not assume a Chinese policy reader will recognise it as a term of art.

translations.notes: Used in the Chinese text of the IDAIS Beijing consensus, paired with 灾难性 exactly as English pairs 'catastrophic' with 'existential'. The -性 suffix blocks the 'a firm's survival' reading better than bare 生存风险. Recommended.

attestations.quote_zh: 人工智能系统不安全的开发、部署或使用，在我们的有生之年就可能给人类带来灾难性甚至生存性风险。
attestations.quote_en: Unsafe development, deployment or use of AI systems may bring catastrophic or even existential risks to humanity within our lifetimes.
attestations.source_title: 北京 AI 安全国际共识（IDAIS-Beijing）
attestations.publisher: 北京智源人工智能研究院 (BAAI) / IDAIS

translations.notes: Chinese Wikipedia's headword for the concept (通用人工智能的生存风险). Most widely recognised of the candidates, but see pitfalls — the ordinary-language 'organisational survival' reading is strong.

attestations.quote_zh: 通用人工智能的生存风险是假设通用人工智能的重大进展可能导致人类灭绝或其他一些无法逆转的全球灾难。
attestations.quote_en: Existential risk from AGI is the hypothesis that major progress in artificial general intelligence could lead to human extinction or some other irreversible global catastrophe.
attestations.source_title: 通用人工智能的生存风险
attestations.publisher: 维基百科（中文）

translations.literal_back: risk at the level of survival
translations.notes: Periphrastic form used in Chinese reporting of the 2025 IDAIS Shanghai consensus. Evidence that even signatory-level documents sometimes decline to commit to a fixed noun.

attestations.quote_zh: 一个或多个通用人工智能系统脱离任何人的控制，从而带来灾难性甚至是生存层面的风险。
attestations.quote_en: One or more AGI systems escaping anyone's control, thereby bringing catastrophic or even existential-level risks.
attestations.source_title: 辛顿、姚期智等联名签署“上海共识”，呼吁给AI确立行为红线
attestations.publisher: 澎湃新闻

translations.notes: The most literal calque of 'existential', and it does circulate in translated philosophy. Recommend against it in running prose: 存在 as an ordinary verb makes 存在风险 readable as 'there is a risk', which inverts the emphasis entirely.

Unambiguous and vivid, but strictly narrower than the English — existential risk includes unrecoverable non-extinction outcomes. Use when the source says 'extinction risk'. No attestation of the noun 灭绝风险 was located in this pass: the Chinese International AI Safety Report, previously cited here, uses 灭绝 only descriptively (人类被边缘化甚至灭绝, 像人类灭绝这种极端后果) and contains zero occurrences of 灭绝风险.

used_by.org: 北京智源人工智能研究院 (BAAI) / IDAIS
used_by.note: 北京 AI 安全国际共识, 2024-03
article headword
no x-risk noun; renders the concept descriptively via 灭绝 / 极端后果

used_by.org: 全国网络安全标准化技术委员会 (TC260)
used_by.note: no equivalent term in 《人工智能安全治理框架》 1.0/2.0

usage_examples.zh: 有些专家认为，像人类灭绝这种极端后果有可能会发生。
usage_examples.en: Some experts believe extreme outcomes such as human extinction are possible.

definition_en: The pre-LLM research tradition of producing human-legible explanations for model decisions — saliency maps, LIME, SHAP, feature attribution, surrogate models — largely motivated by high-stakes deployment (medicine, credit, justice) rather than by misalignment risk.
definition_zh: 大模型之前就存在的研究传统，目标是为模型的单次决策给出人能看懂的解释：显著图、LIME、SHAP、特征归因、代理模型等。它的动机主要是医疗、信贷、司法等高风险场景下的问责，而不是失控风险。
pitfalls: Not a translation problem but a discourse-mapping problem. Chinese academia has a large, mature XAI literature (《计算机研究与发展》, 《计算机学报》, 南大/浙大 groups) predating the Anthropic lineage by years, and it owns the phrase 可解释性. A Chinese reader who hears 可解释性 will by default picture LIME/SHAP/显著图, not SAEs and circuits. Anyone importing mech-interp vocabulary into Chinese is speaking into a room that already has a different referent for the umbrella word. The bare acronym XAI is used untranslated very freely.

translations.notes: Standard in Chinese academic writing since roughly 2019. Often written 可解释人工智能（XAI）; the bare acronym XAI is then reused throughout.
The acronym is used bare in Chinese sentences with no expansion, exactly as in English.

used_by.org: 《计算机研究与发展》(中科院计算所)
used_by.zh_used: 可解释性 / 可解释人工智能
used_by.note: multiple survey articles 2019-2020

usage_examples.zh: 早期的可解释人工智能主要靠显著图和 SHAP 值，解释的是单次预测，而不是模型内部的算法。
usage_examples.en: Early explainable AI relied mainly on saliency maps and SHAP values; it explained a single prediction, not the algorithm inside the model.

definition_en: Restrictions on cross-border transfer of controlled items. In AI they cover advanced chips and manufacturing equipment, and — briefly, under a January 2025 US rule rescinded in May 2025 — model weights themselves.
definition_zh: 对受管制物项跨境转移的限制。在人工智能领域主要针对先进芯片和制造设备；2025 年 1 月美国商务部工业与安全局曾试图将模型权重本身纳入管制，该规则于同年 5 月被废除。
pitfalls: The term itself is a clean one-to-one match and needs no explanation. What does not carry over is the framing: in PRC official texts 出口管制 by other states is routinely characterised as 单边强制措施 (unilateral coercive measures) that 制造发展壁垒 (create development barriers). Using the term neutrally in a Chinese-language safety argument is fine, but expect the political valence to be read in. Note also 管制 (control, restrictive) vs 管理 (administration) vs 监管 (supervision) — 管制 is the strongest of the three.

translations.notes: The standard legal term, also the name of the PRC's own 《出口管制法》. Universal across policy, media and technical writing.

attestations.quote_zh: 但个别国家利用技术垄断和出口管制等单边强制措施制造发展壁垒，恶意阻断全球人工智能供应链，带来突出的芯片、软件、工具断供风险。
attestations.quote_en: However, certain countries use unilateral coercive measures such as technological monopoly and export controls to create barriers to development, maliciously cutting off the global AI supply chain and creating acute risks of chip, software and tooling cut-off.
attestations.source_title: 《人工智能安全治理框架》2.0 版
attestations.publisher: 全国网络安全标准化技术委员会 (TC260) / 国家计算机网络应急技术处理协调中心

attestations.quote_zh: 2025 年 1 月，商务部工业与安全局（BIS）首次发布规则，试图将 AI 模型权重本身纳入出口管制，但该规则在 5 月被新政府以“扼杀创新”为由废除。
attestations.quote_en: In January 2025 the Bureau of Industry and Security (BIS) issued a rule for the first time attempting to bring AI model weights themselves within export controls, but the rule was rescinded in May by the new administration on the grounds that it 'stifled innovation'.
attestations.source_title: 人工智能治理研究报告（2025 年）
attestations.publisher: 中国信息通信研究院（CAICT）政策与经济研究所

attestations.quote_zh: 评估模型或系统是否能提供专业知识（包括与云实验室合作、隐藏 DNA 合成订单、规避出口管制、检索并分析危险 DNA 序列等），协助相关行为主体获取制造生物威胁或生物武器所需的材料和设备。
attestations.quote_en: Assess whether the model or system can provide expertise — including working with cloud labs, concealing DNA synthesis orders, evading export controls, and retrieving and analysing dangerous DNA sequences — to help actors obtain the materials and equipment needed to make biological threats or weapons.
attestations.source_title: 《前沿人工智能风险管理框架 2.0》
attestations.publisher: 上海人工智能实验室 / 安远 AI (Concordia AI)

used_by.note: in the 2.0 framework's framing of supply-chain risk
throughout its 2025 AI governance report

usage_examples.zh: 把模型权重纳入出口管制，在技术上比管制芯片困难得多。
usage_examples.en: Bringing model weights under export controls is technically far harder than controlling chips.

definition_en: In mechanistic interpretability, a direction in a model's activation space that corresponds to a human-legible concept and serves as the basic unit of computation — not an input variable and not a neuron.
definition_zh: 在机制可解释性里，特征指激活空间中的一个方向，它对应一个人类能理解的概念，并作为模型计算的基本单元。它既不是输入变量，也不等于某个神经元。
pitfalls: 特征 is the correct word but it is badly overloaded, and the overload is worse in Chinese than in English because Chinese has no separate everyday word for 'trait'. In classical ML 特征 = input variable (特征工程 = feature engineering), and the whole XAI tradition uses 特征归因 = feature attribution over input features. The mech-interp sense — a learned direction, discovered rather than designed — is a different object. Chinese writers disambiguate ad hoc: 特征单元, SAE 特征, 可解释特征, 稀疏特征, or keep the English 'feature' in parentheses. 'Latent' as a synonym is not usually rendered; 潜变量/隐变量 would be read as VAE latents.

translations.notes: Universal, but usually qualified (SAE 特征 / 可解释特征 / 稀疏特征 / 特征单元) when the interp sense is meant.

attestations.quote_zh: 第一步，识别特征——特征指的是模型在计算中使用的可被解释的构建模块。
attestations.quote_en: Step one, identify features — features are the interpretable building blocks the model uses in its computation.
attestations.source_title: Anthropic提出工作回路追踪方法：用归因图解开大语言模型计算之谜
attestations.publisher: 集智俱乐部

attestations.quote_zh: 该方法包括两步，首先，将特征作为识别模型计算中使用的可解释基础单元。其次，描述这些特征如何通过过程或回路相互作用以产生模型输出。
attestations.quote_en: The method has two steps: first, treat features as the interpretable basic units used in the model's computation; second, describe how these features interact through processes or circuits to produce the model's output.
attestations.source_title: Anthropic AI 最新研究成果发布：揭示大模型中的注意力回路
attestations.publisher: 雷峰网 (洪雨欣)

translations.notes: A useful disambiguating variant when 特征 alone would read as 'input feature'.

attestations.quote_zh: SAE 会解构出若干稀疏激活的'特征单元'（feature）
attestations.quote_en: The SAE decomposes things into a number of sparsely activating 'feature units'.
attestations.source_title: 大模型到底是怎么「思考」的？第一篇系统性综述SAE的文章来了
attestations.publisher: 机器之心Pro (via 新浪科技)

used_by.note: in its 大模型可解释性读书会 materials

usage_examples.zh: 这里说的特征不是输入变量，而是激活空间中的一个方向。
usage_examples.en: The features here are not input variables but directions in activation space.

definition_en: Intervening on an identified interpretable feature — clamping its activation up or down — to change model behaviour in a targeted way, as in Golden Gate Claude.
definition_zh: 对已经识别出来的可解释特征直接干预——把它的激活值强行调高或压低——从而定向改变模型行为，Golden Gate Claude 就是典型例子。
pitfalls: Not settled. 引导 (guide/steer) is the verb Chinese survey writing uses for 'steering' in general, giving 特征引导 / 特征级引导, and this is our recommendation. But 操控 (manipulate/control) is also widely used — 模型操控 for 'model steering' — and it is more forceful, carrying a hint of illegitimate manipulation that 'steering' does not. 干预 (intervene) is a third, more neutral option. Note the collision risk with 激活引导 (activation steering), a related but distinct technique in the alignment-techniques category: 特征引导 specifically presupposes SAE features, 激活引导 does not.

translations.notes: Our recommendation. The 引导 stem matches the way Chinese surveys render the 'locate, steer, improve' pipeline (定位、引导与改进).
Used for 'model steering' generally. More forceful than 引导 and slightly pejorative in ordinary Chinese; prefer 引导 in safety writing where the connotation matters. No fetchable verbatim recovered.

usage_examples.zh: 把"金门大桥"这个特征的激活值调到很高，模型就会不停地提到金门大桥。
usage_examples.en: Clamp the 'Golden Gate Bridge' feature's activation high and the model will not stop mentioning the bridge.

definition_en: A model trained on broad data at scale and designed to be adapted to a wide range of downstream tasks. Stanford CRFM coinage, now standard in regulation and research.
definition_zh: 指在大规模广泛数据上训练、并被设计成可适配多种下游任务的模型。该术语由斯坦福 CRFM 提出，现已成为研究与监管文本中的标准用语。
pitfalls: Three Chinese words compete and they are not synonyms. 基础模型 is the correct rendering of 'foundation model' and is what official translations use. 基座模型 is a practitioner term meaning specifically the pretrained-but-not-yet-aligned base checkpoint — closer to English 'base model' than to 'foundation model'; translating 'foundation model' as 基座模型 wrongly narrows it to the pre-finetuning artefact. 大模型 is a Chinese-origin umbrella term ('large model') with no clean English equivalent: it covers foundation models, LLMs, multimodal models and, loosely, the whole product category, and it is by far the most frequent word in Chinese industry writing. Translating 大模型 back into English almost always requires choosing a narrower English term than the Chinese author committed to — a genuine asymmetry running in the ZH→EN direction.

translations.notes: The rendering used in the official Chinese International AI Safety Report glossary. Recommended for 'foundation model' in all registers.

attestations.quote_zh: 基础模型（Foundation model）：一款通用型人工智能模型，旨在适应广泛的下游任务。
attestations.quote_en: Foundation model: a general-purpose AI model intended to be adapted to a wide range of downstream tasks.
attestations.source_title: 《2026 年国际人工智能安全报告》（中文版）词汇表
attestations.publisher: International AI Safety Report（主席 Yoshua Bengio）

translations.notes: Practitioner term for the pretrained base checkpoint before fine-tuning. Chinese explainers explicitly distinguish it from 基础模型. Use for English 'base model', not for 'foundation model'.

attestations.quote_zh: 基座模型一般指大数据预训练过但是没有微调的模型；而基础模型就是日常所说的“大模型”
attestations.quote_en: A jizuo model generally means a model that has been pretrained on large data but not fine-tuned; a jichu model is what people ordinarily call a 'large model'.
attestations.source_title: 什么是大模型？超大模型和 Foundation Model 呢？
attestations.publisher: 知乎

translations.notes: Chinese-origin umbrella term with no clean English equivalent — covers foundation models, LLMs and the broader product category. Dominant in Chinese industry and media writing. Record it as the source term when translating ZH→EN rather than assuming it means 'foundation model'.

attestations.quote_zh: 大型语言模型（英語：large language model，LLM），也称大语言模型，简称大模型，是一種基於人工神经网络的语言模型。
attestations.quote_en: A large language model (LLM), also called da yuyan moxing and abbreviated da moxing, is a language model based on artificial neural networks.
attestations.source_title: 大型语言模型
attestations.publisher: 维基百科（中文）

used_by.note: glossary
reports on Chinese 基础模型 developers signing safety commitments

usage_examples.zh: 国内主流基础模型厂商大多已签署《人工智能安全承诺》。
usage_examples.en: Most mainstream domestic foundation-model developers have signed the AI Safety Commitment.

definition_en: Rules aimed specifically at the most capable general-purpose models, usually triggered by a capability or compute threshold rather than by application sector.
definition_zh: 专门针对能力最强的通用人工智能模型的监管规则，通常以能力或算力阈值（而非应用行业）作为触发条件。
pitfalls: 前沿人工智能 is a settled term, but the *regulatory category* it names in English has no PRC counterpart. Chinese regulation is organised by 分类分级监管 (classified and graded oversight) keyed to application scenario, 智能化水平 and 应用规模 — not by a 'frontier' tier. So 前沿人工智能监管 reads to a PRC policy audience as a description of foreign (EU/UK/US) practice rather than a domestic instrument. Also note 监管 (regulation by a state organ) vs 治理 (governance, multi-stakeholder) vs 管理 (administration): choosing 监管 makes the claim that a regulator is doing it.

translations.notes: The head term is fully settled in Chinese AI-safety writing; 前沿大模型 (frontier large model) is a common variant in policy prose.

attestations.quote_zh: 上海人工智能实验室联合安远 AI，于 2025 年 7 月正式发布《前沿人工智能风险管理框架（1.0 版）》，旨在为通用型人工智能模型开发者提供全面的风险管理指导方针。
attestations.quote_en: Shanghai AI Laboratory, together with Concordia AI, formally released the Frontier AI Risk Management Framework (v1.0) in July 2025, aiming to give developers of general-purpose AI models comprehensive risk-management guidance.
attestations.source_title: 《前沿人工智能风险管理框架 2.0》
attestations.publisher: 上海人工智能实验室 / 安远 AI (Concordia AI)

translations.notes: Compositional and readily understood, but not a fixed PRC policy category; I could not recover it as a set phrase in an authoritative Chinese source. Use it for describing EU/UK/US regimes.

The PRC-native alternative that occupies the same policy slot: instead of carving out a 'frontier' tier, TC260 and CAC grade all AI applications by scenario, intelligence level and deployment scale. Not a synonym — record both and say which system you are describing.

attestations.quote_zh: 推动人工智能安全相关立法，完善基础设施安全防护、分级分类监管、人工智能安全测评、最终用途管理、重点场景安全应用等制度。
attestations.quote_en: Advance legislation on AI safety, and improve systems for infrastructure security protection, graded and classified oversight, AI safety evaluation, end-use management and safe application in key scenarios.
attestations.source_title: 《人工智能安全治理框架》2.0 版
attestations.publisher: 全国网络安全标准化技术委员会 (TC260) / 国家计算机网络应急技术处理协调中心

used_by.org: 上海人工智能实验室 / 安远 AI
used_by.note: title of their risk-management framework
the PRC's structural alternative to a frontier tier

usage_examples.zh: 欧盟以算力阈值触发前沿人工智能监管，我国则以应用场景和智能化水平进行分级分类监管。
usage_examples.en: The EU triggers frontier AI regulation via a compute threshold, whereas China grades and classifies oversight by application scenario and level of autonomy.

definition_en: Voluntary commitments signed by 16 AI companies at the AI Seoul Summit on 21 May 2024: publish a safety framework, define capability thresholds at which risks become intolerable, and set out mitigations — including not developing or deploying a model at all if the risks cannot be brought below the thresholds. Zhipu AI was the Chinese signatory.
definition_zh: 2024 年 5 月 21 日人工智能首尔峰会上由 16 家人工智能企业签署的自愿性承诺，要求公开安全框架、界定风险不可容忍的能力阈值并说明缓解措施，包括在风险无法降至阈值以下时不开发或不部署模型。智谱 AI 是其中唯一的中国签署方。
preferred_zh: 前沿人工智能安全承诺
pitfalls: Straightforward, and Chinese coverage carries the English name in parentheses. The thing to flag is that a separate, PRC-domestic instrument exists with a confusingly similar name: 《人工智能安全承诺》 / 《中国人工智能安全承诺框架》, a voluntary commitment led by CAICT and signed by 22 domestic foundation-model developers. Do not conflate the two — the Seoul commitments are an international, frontier-risk instrument; the CAICT one is a domestic industry self-discipline framework.

translations.zh: 前沿人工智能安全承诺
translations.notes: Used with the English name attached on first mention in Chinese coverage.

attestations.quote_zh: 此次峰会上，智谱AI 同来自北美、亚洲、欧洲和中东地区的 15 家顶级人工智能公司一道就AI开发安全承诺达成一致，签署前沿人工智能安全承诺（Frontier AI Safety Commitments）。
attestations.quote_en: At the summit, Zhipu AI joined 15 leading AI companies from North America, Asia, Europe and the Middle East in agreeing on safety commitments for AI development and signing the Frontier AI Safety Commitments.
attestations.source_title: 中国智谱AI与OpenAI等公司共同签署前沿人工智能安全承诺
attestations.publisher: 中国日报中文网

attestations.quote_zh: 前沿人工智能安全承诺主要包括确保前沿人工智能安全的负责任治理结构和透明度、基于人工智能安全框架、负责任地说明将如何衡量前沿人工智能模型的风险以及建立前沿人工智能安全模型风险缓解机制的明确流程。
attestations.quote_en: The Frontier AI Safety Commitments mainly cover responsible governance structures and transparency for frontier AI safety, safety frameworks, responsible accounts of how frontier model risks will be measured, and clear processes for establishing risk-mitigation mechanisms.

definition_en: A highly capable general-purpose model at or near the current capability frontier, whose novel capabilities may pose risks not present in earlier systems. Load-bearing in frontier-safety frameworks and in regulation.
definition_zh: 指能力处于或接近当前技术前沿的高能力通用模型，其新增能力可能带来以往系统所没有的风险。这一概念在前沿安全框架和监管文件中承担着划定适用范围的作用。
pitfalls: Unproblematic as a calque, but note the scope split: 前沿模型 names the artefact, 前沿人工智能 names the class of systems, and 前沿大模型 is the practitioner form that folds in the Chinese 大模型 umbrella. Regulatory texts should follow the source's choice, since in frontier-safety frameworks the distinction between model and system determines what the obligations attach to.

translations.notes: Standard in the official Chinese International AI Safety Report, including in the rendering of the Frontier Model Forum's name.

attestations.quote_zh: 对生产能力、投资和技术进步等限制因素的分析表明，前沿模型所使用的算力有望以当前速度持续增长，而不会在芯片制造或能源生产方面触及根本性瓶颈。

definition_en: The genre of document in which a frontier developer commits in advance to evaluating for specified dangerous capabilities, defines thresholds, and states what safeguards or halts follow when a threshold is crossed. Google DeepMind's document carries this exact name; OpenAI's is the Preparedness Framework, Anthropic's the RSP.
definition_zh: 前沿开发者预先承诺的一类文件：约定要评测哪些危险能力、设定相应阈值，并规定阈值被触发后必须采取的防护措施或暂停动作。谷歌DeepMind的同名文件叫《前沿安全框架》，OpenAI的叫《应急准备框架》，Anthropic的则是RSP。
pitfalls: Chinese has done something English has not: it has separated the proper noun from the genre. 前沿安全框架 is used specifically for Google DeepMind's document, while the umbrella category is 前沿AI风险管理框架 / 前沿人工智能风险管理框架 — the phrasing Concordia AI uses to cover all five labs, and the title of the Chinese-origin framework issued by Shanghai AI Lab with Concordia AI in July 2025. If you write 前沿安全框架 when you mean the genre, a well-read Chinese reader will think you mean DeepMind's. Note also that the Chinese umbrella term foregrounds 风险管理 (risk management), aligning the genre with ISO-style enterprise risk management rather than with 'safety' as a distinct value — a framing choice that makes the genre legible to PRC regulators. There is a native Chinese instance of this genre, which matters: 上海人工智能实验室 and 安远AI's framework uses a 红线/黄线 two-tier threshold system rather than importing ASL-style numbered levels.

translations.notes: Used as the proper name of Google DeepMind's document in both the International AI Safety Report Chinese edition and Concordia AI's writing.
