definition_en: In the PRC a statutorily defined category. Article 2 of the 2015 National Security Law defines 国家安全 as the state of relative freedom from danger and from internal or external threat to state power, sovereignty, unity and territorial integrity, the people's welfare, sustainable economic and social development and other major national interests — together with the capacity to keep that state secure. The law and the 总体国家安全观 (holistic approach to national security) built on it span political, territorial, military, economic, cultural, social, technological, cyber, ecological, nuclear and further domains. The 2015 law itself does not name artificial intelligence; AI enters the category through the doctrine's later enumerations and through planning documents such as the 2025 Fourth Plenum recommendations, which call for building national security capability in emerging fields including AI.
definition_zh: 在中国，国家安全是有法律定义的范畴。《国家安全法》第二条规定，国家安全是指国家政权、主权、统一和领土完整、人民福祉、经济社会可持续发展和国家其他重大利益相对处于没有危险和不受内外威胁的状态，以及保障持续安全状态的能力。该法与在其基础上展开的“总体国家安全观”涵盖政治、国土、军事、经济、文化、社会、科技、网络、生态、核等诸多领域。2015 年法律文本本身并未出现“人工智能”；人工智能是通过总体国家安全观后续的领域列举，以及二十届四中全会建议等规划文件中“加强人工智能等新兴领域国家安全能力建设”的表述进入这一范畴的。
pitfalls: Lexically trivial, politically the most load-bearing term in the category. Three consequences for anyone writing AI-safety arguments in Chinese. (1) 国家安全 in the PRC is a defined legal category with a doctrine (总体国家安全观) and a dedicated legal apparatus; invoking it is not rhetorical framing as it often is in English, it is a jurisdictional claim that pulls a topic into a specific institutional track. (2) It is expressly one of the graded factors in TC260's risk-grading scale, alongside 社会稳定 and 公民权益 — so 'national security risk' has a defined place in Chinese AI risk taxonomy that it lacks in most Western ones. (3) Framing catastrophic-risk arguments as 国家安全 raises their salience but can also make them non-public and non-debatable. Note the systematic pairing with 发展: 统筹发展和安全 and 坚持发展和安全并重 are the standard formulations, and any argument that reads as anti-development will be discounted.

translations.notes: One-to-one lexically. What does not transfer is the legal-doctrinal weight; gloss it when the PRC-specific sense matters.

attestations.quote_zh: 严守安全底线，对危害国家安全、社会公共利益、公众合法权益的风险及时采取措施。

attestations.quote_en: In October 2025 the Fourth Plenum of the 20th Central Committee wrote comprehensive implementation of the 'AI+' initiative into the 15th Five-Year Plan recommendations and stressed strengthening national security capability in emerging fields such as AI, marking AI and its governance as fully integrated into national medium- and long-term development strategy.

attestations.quote_zh: 作为两用技术，通用型人工智能有可能被恶意行为者利用，降低非国家行为主体设计、合成、获取和部署化学、生物、放射性、核（以下简称“化生放核”）武器的技术门槛，对国家安全、国际防扩散体系及全球安全治理构成了前所未有的严峻挑战。
attestations.quote_en: As a dual-use technology, general-purpose AI may be exploited by malicious actors to lower the technical barrier for non-state actors to design, synthesise, acquire and deploy chemical, biological, radiological and nuclear weapons, posing unprecedented challenges to national security, the international non-proliferation regime and global security governance.

usage_examples.en: In Chinese policy texts, framing a category of AI risk as a 'national security' issue changes which institutional track it enters.

definition_en: The economic framing, current from late 2023, that places AI, advanced computing and other frontier technologies at the centre of growth policy. It asserts a qualitative — not incremental — change in the productive forces, and is explicitly paired with a corresponding change in the relations of production. It is the slot into which AI is fitted in PRC economic doctrine.
definition_zh: 2023年以来的经济政策提法，把人工智能、先进算力等前沿技术置于增长政策的中心。强调生产力发生的是质的跃迁而非量的积累，并与生产关系的深层次变革相配套，是人工智能在中国经济话语中的定位。
pitfalls: 生产力 is a term of art in historical materialism — the productive forces, paired with 生产关系, the relations of production. English 'productivity' is an output-per-input ratio and is simply a different concept; 'productive forces' is correct but most English readers do not hold the Marxist framework that makes it meaningful. 新质 is 'of a new quality/kind', asserting a categorical break; 'new quality' in English reads as an adjective-noun compound about being high-quality, which is not the claim. The doctrinal pairing is visible in the 2025 AI+ Opinions, which put AI's purpose as 促进生产力革命性跃迁和生产关系深层次变革 — that second clause is a claim about social relations, and it is the part English coverage usually omits.

en_renderings.notes: The settled official and analytic rendering, used both by PRC English-language media and by CSET. Uniformly awkward in English, but stable, and it does at least preserve the Marxist term of art rather than substituting 'productivity'.

attestations.quote_zh: 为深入实施“人工智能+”行动，推动人工智能与经济社会各行业各领域广泛深度融合，重塑人类生产生活范式，促进生产力革命性跃迁和生产关系深层次变革，加快形成人机协同、跨界融合、共创分享的智能经济和智能社会新形态，现提出如下意见。
attestations.quote_en: The following opinions are hereby put forward in order to deeply implement the 'Artificial intelligence+' (AI+) initiative, promote the broad and deep integration of AI across all industries and areas of the economy and society, reshape the paradigms of human production and life, promote a revolutionary leap in the productive forces and profound change in the relations of production …
attestations.source_title: 国务院关于深入实施“人工智能+”行动的意见 / Opinions of the State Council on Deepening the Implementation of the "Artificial Intelligence+" Initiative
attestations.publisher: 国务院 (State Council); English translation by CSET, Georgetown University

attestations.quote_zh: 抓住新一轮科技革命和产业变革历史机遇，统筹教育强国、科技强国、人才强国建设，提升国家创新体系整体效能，全面增强自主创新能力，抢占科技发展制高点，不断催生新质生产力。
attestations.quote_en: Seize the historic opportunity of the new round of technological revolution and industrial transformation … and continually give rise to new quality productive forces (新质生产力).
attestations.source_title: 中共中央关于制定国民经济和社会发展第十五个五年规划的建议
attestations.publisher: 中国政府网 (gov.cn); English translation by CSET, Georgetown University

en_renderings.notes: Appears in some English coverage. Recommend against: it swaps a category of historical materialism for an economic ratio and makes the phrase sound like a management slogan.

why_no_english: The phrase is only interpretable inside a Marxist theory of history that English economic-policy vocabulary abandoned. There is no English word for 'the productive forces' as a historical-stage category, no idiom for asserting that a technology has changed their quality rather than their quantity, and no way to carry the implied second clause about the relations of production. Translations are therefore either literal and opaque, or fluent and wrong about what kind of claim is being made.

en_aliases: new nationwide system for mobilizing resources
new structure for leveraging national capabilities
definition_en: The concentration of national resources — state funding, national labs, leading enterprises, universities — on a small number of designated strategic technology targets. 举国体制 is the older term, associated with Olympic sport and with megaprojects such as the atomic-bomb programme; 新型 marks the version meant to operate 'under the conditions of the socialist market economy', i.e. using firms and markets rather than administrative allocation alone. Directly relevant to compute buildout and to any estimate of how fast PRC AI capacity can be scaled.
definition_zh: 把国家资源集中投向少数战略性技术目标的组织方式，包括国家财政、国家实验室、科技领军企业和高校。“举国体制”原用于体育和“两弹一星”等重大工程；“新型”指在社会主义市场经济条件下运行的版本，即借助企业和市场机制而非单纯行政配置。
pitfalls: 'Whole-of-nation' reads to English ears as an extension of 'whole-of-government', i.e. cross-agency coordination. That is not what 举国 means. 举国 is 'to raise the entire country', to throw everything at one target — the operative gloss in PRC text is 集中力量办大事, 'concentrate strength to accomplish great things', which the 2017 AI Plan explicitly invokes. The system selects targets and starves alternatives; it is about concentration, not coordination. Note also that 新型 is load-bearing and usually dropped in English: the whole point of the qualifier is that this version is supposed to work through market actors, which is what makes it applicable to a commercial AI industry at all.

en_renderings.notes: The most common rendering in English-language analysis and the term an English reader will search for. Its weakness is that 'whole-of-nation' suggests breadth of participation where the Chinese means concentration of resources.

attestations.quote_zh: 完善新型举国体制，采取超常规措施，全链条推动集成电路、工业母机、高端仪器、基础软件、先进材料、生物制造等重点领域关键核心技术攻关取得决定性突破。
attestations.quote_en: Perfect the new whole-of-nation system, adopt extraordinary measures, and drive decisive breakthroughs in key core technologies across the whole chain in priority areas including integrated circuits, machine tools, high-end instruments, basic software, advanced materials and biomanufacturing.
attestations.source_title: 中共中央关于制定国民经济和社会发展第十五个五年规划的建议
attestations.publisher: 中国政府网 (gov.cn)

attestations.quote_zh: 中共中央总书记习近平在主持学习时强调，面对新一代人工智能技术快速演进的新形势，要充分发挥新型举国体制优势，坚持自立自强，突出应用导向，推动我国人工智能朝着有益、安全、公平方向健康有序发展。
attestations.quote_en: … we must give full play to the advantages of the new structure for leveraging national capabilities (新型举国体制), persist in being self-reliant (自立自强), be strongly oriented toward applications, and push the healthy and orderly development of China's AI in a beneficial, safe, and fair direction.
attestations.source_title: 习近平在中共中央政治局第二十次集体学习时强调（新华社通稿）/ CSET translation
attestations.publisher: 新华社 (Xinhua); English translation by CSET, Georgetown University

en_renderings.en: new structure for leveraging national capabilities
en_renderings.notes: CSET's standing rendering. More accurate about what the system does and free of the 'whole-of-government' echo, but long and not established outside CSET's translations.

attestations.quote_zh: 制定科技强国行动纲要，健全社会主义市场经济条件下新型举国体制，打好关键核心技术攻坚战，提高创新链整体效能。
attestations.quote_en: We will formulate an action agenda for becoming an S&T powerhouse, improve the new structure for leveraging national capabilities (新型举国体制) under the conditions of the socialist market economy, successfully fight tough battles [for key core technologies] …
attestations.source_title: 中华人民共和国国民经济和社会发展第十四个五年规划和2035年远景目标纲要 / Outline of the PRC 14th Five-Year Plan
attestations.publisher: 新华社 / 中国政府网; English translation by CSET, Georgetown University

why_no_english: Democratic-market states have wartime mobilisation, moonshot programmes and industrial strategy, but no standing institutional term for a permanent capability to concentrate the nation's resources on designated technology targets. English therefore reaches for either war metaphors (which overstate) or governance jargon (which understates). The additional problem is 新型: English has no compact way to say 'the market-compatible successor version of the planned-economy mobilisation apparatus', so the qualifier that carries the actual analytical content is routinely lost.

used_by.note: 20th Party Congress report, 14th and 15th Five-Year Plan documents
invoked as the organising advantage for AI in the April 2025 Politburo study session

usage_examples.zh: 要充分发挥新型举国体制优势，坚持自立自强，突出应用导向。
usage_examples.en: We must give full play to the advantages of the new whole-of-nation system, persist in self-reliance, and put the emphasis on applications.

usage_examples.zh: 充分发挥社会主义制度集中力量办大事的优势，推进项目、基地、人才统筹布局。
usage_examples.en: Give full play to the socialist system's advantage of concentrating strength to accomplish great things, and plan projects, bases and talent as a whole.

en: open competition to select the best
en_aliases: open competition mechanism to select the best candidates
unveiling the list and taking command
definition_en: A mechanism for allocating state R&D tasks: the government posts a hard technical problem publicly, any qualified team may claim it, and whoever does is appointed to lead the effort with corresponding authority and accountability. Paired in the 14th Five-Year Plan with 赛马 ('horse races', funding several competing teams) as part of a package granting research units more autonomy.
definition_zh: 国家科技任务的组织方式：将攻关任务张榜公布，有能力者揭榜承接，承接者即“挂帅”负责，并被赋予相应的自主权和责任。《十四五规划纲要》将其与“赛马”制并列，作为给予科研单位和科研人员更多自主权的改革措施。
pitfalls: The imagery is imperial-military and does real work: 榜 is a public notice board on which the court posts a task; 揭榜 is tearing that notice down, which is the act of volunteering; 挂帅 is 'to hang out the commander's banner', i.e. to take command. Whoever claims the task becomes its commander. English renderings of the 'open competition' family capture the tendering aspect and lose the command aspect entirely — which is the aspect that distinguishes it from an ordinary grant call. Note also that the seed headword and the CSET rendering are unrelated phrasings for the same term, so an English reader searching one will not find the other.

en_renderings.notes: CSET's rendering in the 14th Five-Year Plan translation, always glossed with the Chinese. It reads 榜 as a ranked list rather than a task notice, which is a defensible but not obvious reading; the merit is that it is attested and consistently glossed.

attestations.quote_zh: 改革重大科技项目立项和组织管理方式，给予科研单位和科研人员更多自主权，推行技术总师负责制，实行“揭榜挂帅”、“赛马”等制度，健全奖补结合的资金支持机制。
attestations.quote_en: We will reform the management methods of major S&T project initiation and organization, grant more autonomy to scientific research units and scientific research personnel, implement a responsibility system for chief technical officers, implement systems such as "announcing rankings" ("揭榜挂帅") and "horse races" ("赛马"), and improve the financial support mechanisms that combine rewards and supplements.
attestations.source_title: 中华人民共和国国民经济和社会发展第十四个五年规划和2035年远景目标纲要 / Outline of the PRC 14th Five-Year Plan
attestations.publisher: 新华社 / 中国政府网; English translation by CSET, Georgetown University

en_renderings.en: open competition to select the best
en_renderings.notes: The rendering most used in English coverage of PRC work reports and the seed headword here. NOT ATTESTED in this research pass — we did not recover a primary official English source for it, so it is recorded on the strength of usage rather than citation, and the entry's confidence is set accordingly.

en_renderings.en: unveil the list and take command
en_renderings.literal_back: tear down the notice, hang the commander's banner
en_renderings.notes: We advocate this where the reader needs to see the mechanism. It preserves the two-step structure — claiming the task and thereby assuming command — which the 'open competition' renderings drop. Not attested.

why_no_english: English research-funding vocabulary — open call, competitive tender, grand challenge, prize competition — describes how money is awarded. 揭榜挂帅 describes how command is transferred: the winner does not merely receive a grant, they are installed as the responsible commander of a national task, with the authority and the exposure that implies. English has no funding term that carries an appointment to lead, because in English-speaking systems the two are administratively separate.

used_by.note: 14th Five-Year Plan outline, paired with 赛马

usage_examples.zh: 实行“揭榜挂帅”、“赛马”等制度，健全奖补结合的资金支持机制。
usage_examples.en: Implement systems such as open-call-and-take-command and horse-racing, and improve funding support mechanisms combining prizes and subsidies.

definition_en: Publishing a model's trained parameters for download, without necessarily publishing training data, training code, or granting an OSI-conformant licence. Distinct from open source, which requires the means to reproduce the artefact.
definition_zh: 把训练好的模型参数公开供下载，但不一定公开训练数据、训练代码，也不一定采用符合开源定义的许可证。与「开源」不同——开源要求提供足以复现该成果的全部要素。
pitfalls: The most consequential terminology problem in this category. Chinese discourse — including the labs themselves — routinely says 开源 (open source) for what is actually a weights release. Qwen's own Chinese release blog writes 我们开源了两个 MoE 模型的权重 ("we open-sourced the weights of two MoE models"), collapsing the distinction in a single phrase; DeepSeek is universally described in Chinese as an 开源大模型. The consequence is that Chinese-language debate about "开源模型" and English-language debate about "open-weight models" are often not about the same object, and a Chinese reader may not register that training data and code were withheld. 开放权重 exists, is correct, and is gaining ground — largely imported through coverage of OpenAI's gpt-oss, which was explicitly marketed as open-weight rather than open-source — but it remains the minority form against the entrenched 开源. When precision matters, write 开放权重（open-weight）and explicitly contrast with 开源.

translations.notes: The precise term. Chinese commentators use it specifically when they want to deny that a release is fully open source. Recommended.

attestations.quote_zh: 虽然开放权重并非严格意义上的开源，但它赋予了AI技术透明性
attestations.quote_en: Although open weights is not open source in the strict sense, it grants AI technology transparency.
attestations.source_title: 大模型时代的开源：从开放代码到开放权重的演进
attestations.publisher: Jimmy Song《智能体构建指南》

attestations.quote_zh: 开放权重 ≠ 完全开源
attestations.quote_en: Open weights ≠ fully open source.
attestations.source_title: 大模型时代的开源：从开放代码到开放权重的演进
attestations.publisher: Jimmy Song《智能体构建指南》

translations.notes: By far the dominant Chinese usage, and the one to argue against. Chinese labs describe weight releases as 开源, which is what makes the pitfall load-bearing rather than pedantic. Recorded as deprecated for precision work, not because it is rare — it is the default. Recorded in research as “开源（模型）”.

attestations.quote_zh: 我们开源了两个 MoE 模型的权重：Qwen3-235B-A22B，一个拥有 2350 多亿总参数和 220 多亿激活参数的大模型
attestations.quote_en: We open-sourced the weights of two MoE models: Qwen3-235B-A22B, a large model with over 235 billion total parameters and over 22 billion activated parameters.
attestations.source_title: Qwen3: 思深，行速
attestations.publisher: 阿里巴巴通义千问 (Qwen)

used_by.note: conflates the two in its own Chinese release blog

usage_examples.zh: 严格来说它只是开放权重，训练数据和训练代码都没公开，不算完全开源。
usage_examples.en: Strictly speaking it is only open-weight: neither the training data nor the training code was released, so it isn't fully open source.

definition_en: Bostrom's claim that an agent's level of intelligence and its final goals are independent axes: any level of capability can in principle be combined with any goal, so being smarter does not make a system's goals more humane.
definition_zh: 博斯特罗姆提出的论点：智能水平与最终目标是两个相互独立的维度，任意水平的智能原则上可以与任意目标相结合，因此系统更聪明并不意味着它的目标更符合人类价值。
pitfalls: Unproblematic. 正交 is the standard mathematical 'orthogonal' and the metaphor transfers cleanly. 论点 (thesis/claim) and 论题 both circulate; 假设 (hypothesis) is weaker than the English and slightly misrepresents it. The term is largely confined to translated-Bostrom material and academic surveys — it is not part of working ML vocabulary in Chinese.

translations.notes: Used with the English term glossed in parentheses in the standard Chinese LLM-alignment survey. 正交性论题 is an equally acceptable variant.

attestations.quote_zh: 正交性论点（Orthogonality Thesis）：该论点认为AI代理的智能和它的目标处于两个正交的维度，即任意水平的智能可以与任意的目标相结合（Bostrom, 2012），处于高智能水平的AI代理并不意味着其目标与人类价值对齐。
attestations.quote_en: Orthogonality Thesis: this thesis holds that an AI agent's intelligence and its goals lie on two orthogonal dimensions, i.e. any level of intelligence can be combined with any goal (Bostrom, 2012); a highly intelligent AI agent does not thereby have goals aligned with human values.
attestations.source_title: 《大语言模型对齐：概念、挑战、路线、评测及趋势》
attestations.publisher: 熊德意（天津大学），第二十二届中国计算语言学大会论文集（CCL 2023），中国中文信息学会

used_by.org: 天津大学 熊德意组
used_by.note: CCL 2023 frontier survey

usage_examples.zh: 按照正交性论点，系统能力再强，也不能推出它的目标是善的。
usage_examples.en: By the orthogonality thesis, no matter how capable a system is, it does not follow that its goals are good.

definition_en: Whether the training objective actually written down captures what humans intended. Outer alignment failures are specification problems: the reward is a proxy, and optimizing the proxy diverges from the goal.
definition_zh: 指实际写下来的训练目标，是否真的表达了人类想要的东西。外部对齐失败属于规范问题：奖励只是代理指标，把代理指标优化到极致就会偏离真正的目标。
pitfalls: Settled and unproblematic. Note that Chinese sources classify RLHF as an outer-alignment method and explicitly call human preference a 替代物（Proxy）for human values — useful vocabulary when explaining why outer alignment is hard. As with inner alignment, the negative form 外部未对齐 also circulates.

translations.notes: Glossed with 'Outer Alignment' on first use in the standard Chinese survey.

attestations.quote_zh: 外部对齐（Outer Alignment）：人类价值或预期目标与AI模型训练目标之间的对齐，即AI代理的设计人员是否将人类价值/预期目标转化对应到AI代理的训练目标函数上。
attestations.quote_en: Outer alignment: alignment between human values or intended goals and the AI model's training objective, i.e. whether the AI agent's designers have translated human values/intended goals into the agent's training objective function.
attestations.source_title: 《大语言模型对齐：概念、挑战、路线、评测及趋势》
attestations.publisher: 熊德意（天津大学），第二十二届中国计算语言学大会论文集（CCL 2023），中国中文信息学会

attestations.quote_zh: 与此相反，人类反馈强化学习RLHF则进行了外部对齐，对齐的实际目标是人类价值、意图等
attestations.quote_en: By contrast, RLHF does perform outer alignment; the actual target of alignment is human values, intentions and so on.
attestations.source_title: 《大语言模型对齐：概念、挑战、路线、评测及趋势》
attestations.publisher: 熊德意（天津大学），第二十二届中国计算语言学大会论文集（CCL 2023），中国中文信息学会

used_by.org: 天津大学 熊德意组
used_by.note: CCL 2023 frontier survey

usage_examples.zh: RLHF 属于外部对齐方法，它用人类偏好作为人类价值的替代物。
usage_examples.en: RLHF is an outer-alignment method; it uses human preference as a proxy for human values.

definition_en: The situation where mechanisms intended to keep humans able to review, correct or stop an AI system stop working — because the system is too fast, too opaque, too numerous, or because reviewers rubber-stamp.
definition_zh: 本应让人类能够审查、纠正或叫停 AI 系统的机制失去效力：或因系统太快、太不透明、数量太多，或因审查者流于形式。
pitfalls: No fixed Chinese term. Chinese discourse reaches for adjacent words instead, and each shifts the meaning: 失控 ('loss of control') is the overwhelmingly dominant framing but describes the system going out of control, not the oversight mechanism breaking down; 监管失灵 means regulatory failure at the institutional level, not operator-level oversight; 人工干预失效 is closest but rare. The English concept — oversight exists on paper but does not bite — is not lexicalised in Chinese and normally has to be written out as a clause (人类实际上已无法有效监督/纠正). Recording this as a gap rather than proposing a calque with confidence.

translations.notes: Proposed here as the most transparent compositional rendering: 监督 matches the 人类监督 used in Chinese translations of the EU AI Act, and 失效 is the standard word for a safeguard ceasing to function. Not attested as a fixed term in the sources reviewed; offered as a coinage, not a report of usage.

What Chinese sources actually say. Broader and more dramatic than 'oversight failure' — it names the outcome (the system is out of control) rather than the mechanism (nobody was effectively checking). Do not treat as an equivalent; see the loss-of-control entry.

attestations.quote_zh: 催生了指令注入、越权操作、技能供应链攻击、智能体失控等新型安全隐患
attestations.quote_en: …giving rise to new safety hazards such as prompt injection, privilege-exceeding operations, skill supply-chain attacks and agent loss of control.
attestations.source_title: 智能体安全研究员（招聘页）
attestations.publisher: 安远 AI (Concordia AI)

attestations.quote_zh: 智能体可以自主决策，又能通过与环境交互施加对物理世界影响，一旦失控将给人类社会带来极大威胁。
attestations.quote_en: Agents can decide autonomously and can affect the physical world by interacting with their environment; once they get out of control they pose an enormous threat to human society.
attestations.source_title: 警惕人工智能时代的“智能体风险”
attestations.publisher: 新华社 / 新华网

usage_examples.zh: 流程上写着要人工审批，实际上审批只是点一下，人类监督已经形同虚设。
usage_examples.en: The process says manual approval is required, but approval is just a click — human oversight has become a formality.

definition_en: A motor-racing metaphor: you cannot pass a faster car on the straight, so you gain on the corner. In technology policy it means seizing a moment of technological discontinuity — a disruptive technology that zeroes out the incumbent's accumulated advantage in investment, talent, industry and rules — to move ahead of a leader you could not out-run on the existing track.
definition_zh: 赛车比喻：直道上追不上，就在弯道超越。用于科技政策，指抓住颠覆性技术带来的不连续窗口，使现有投资、人才、技术、产业、规则的积累优势“归零”，从而实现对领先者的赶超。
pitfalls: 'Leapfrogging' is the nearest English term but means something different: skipping a technology generation, typically in a development-economics sense (going straight to mobile without landlines). 弯道超车 is not about skipping a stage; it is about exploiting a discontinuity in which the leader's advantage is temporarily neutralised. The literal 'overtaking on the curve' preserves the image but is opaque without the racing frame. Register is the other issue: this is commentary and speech vocabulary, common in Chinese AI discussion, but it is markedly less present in top-level policy text — see the usage note below before treating an instance as an official position.

en_renderings.notes: The literal rendering and the one an English reader will meet. The 2016 National Innovation-Driven Development Strategy Outline uses it in quotation marks, tied explicitly to disruptive technologies that zero out incumbent advantage.

attestations.quote_zh: 高度关注可能引起现有投资、人才、技术、产业、规则“归零”的颠覆性技术，前瞻布局新兴产业前沿技术研发，力争实现“弯道超车”。
attestations.quote_en: Pay close attention to disruptive technologies that could 'zero out' existing investment, talent, technology, industry and rules; lay out forward-looking R&D in frontier technologies for emerging industries, and strive to achieve 'overtaking on the curve'.
attestations.source_title: 《国家创新驱动发展战略纲要》
attestations.publisher: 中共中央、国务院 (CCP Central Committee and State Council), via 中国政府网

en_renderings.notes: Recommend against as a straight substitute. It names a different mechanism (skipping a generation) and carries development-economics connotations the Chinese does not have.

why_no_english: English technology-strategy vocabulary has 'first-mover advantage', 'fast follower', 'leapfrogging' and 'disruption', but nothing for the specific move of waiting for a discontinuity because you cannot win on the current track. The racing metaphor also supplies a competitor and a track — an explicitly relative, two-party framing — where English disruption vocabulary is about markets rather than rivals.

used_by.note: 2016 National Innovation-Driven Development Strategy Outline, in quotation marks

usage_examples.zh: 前瞻布局新兴产业前沿技术研发，力争实现“弯道超车”。
usage_examples.en: Lay out forward-looking R&D in frontier technologies for emerging industries and strive to overtake on the curve.

definition_en: A general Party formulation — 'take people as the root' — that opens most PRC AI ethics and governance documents. In the Global AI Governance Initiative it is given operative content: AI development is to aim at the common wellbeing of humanity, on the premise of safeguarding social security and respecting human rights and interests. Outside AI, the identical four characters govern urbanisation policy and talent policy.
definition_zh: 党的一般性提法，字面意为“以人为根本”，是中国人工智能伦理与治理文件的标准开篇表述。《全球人工智能治理倡议》赋予其具体内容：以增进人类共同福祉为目标，以保障社会安全、尊重人类权益为前提。同样四字也用于新型城镇化、人才政策等领域。
pitfalls: Assess this one carefully before treating it as the PRC counterpart of 'human-centred AI'. It is a general-purpose Party formula, not an AI design principle: the 15th Five-Year Plan Recommendations use it for 以人为本的新型城镇化 (people-centred new urbanisation) and the 2016 innovation strategy uses it for talent policy. So its appearance at the head of an AI document is at least partly formulaic. That said, it is not empty — the Global AI Governance Initiative attaches specific conditions to it. Two further traps: 人 is collective (the people, humanity), not the individual user, so 'human-centred' in the HCI sense is a false friend in the reverse direction; and 以人为本 should be distinguished from the adjacent official formula 以人民为中心, which is more explicitly political.

en_renderings.notes: This is the official English. The PRC's own translation of the Global AI Governance Initiative gives 'uphold a people-centered approach in developing AI'. CSET uses the same word for the non-AI uses. Use it, and reserve 'human-centred' for the English-origin HCI concept to avoid collapsing the two.

attestations.quote_zh: ——发展人工智能应坚持“以人为本”理念，以增进人类共同福祉为目标，以保障社会安全、尊重人类权益为前提，确保人工智能始终朝着有利于人类文明进步的方向发展。
attestations.quote_en: We should uphold a people-centered approach in developing AI, with the goal of increasing the wellbeing of humanity and on the premise of ensuring social security and respecting the rights and interests of humanity, so that AI always develops in a way that is beneficial to human civilization.
attestations.source_title: 《全球人工智能治理倡议》 / Global AI Governance Initiative
attestations.publisher: 国家互联网信息办公室 (CAC); official English via Embassy of the PRC in the USA

attestations.quote_zh: （31）深入推进以人为本的新型城镇化。
attestations.quote_en: (31) Deeply advance people-centered (以人为本) new urbanization.
attestations.source_title: 中共中央关于制定国民经济和社会发展第十五个五年规划的建议
attestations.publisher: 中国政府网 (gov.cn); English translation by CSET, Georgetown University

en_renderings.notes: Recommend against for PRC documents. It imports the human-centred-AI / human-centred-design tradition, which is about individual users and interaction, whereas 人 here is collective and the referent is the wellbeing of humanity and social order. Using it makes a Party formula look like a design methodology.

why_no_english: The difficulty is not lexical but pragmatic. 以人为本 is a doctrinal opening move: a document establishes its legitimacy by declaring the canonical formula before saying anything specific. English policy documents have no slot for that gesture, so the phrase arrives in translation looking like a substantive commitment when a Chinese reader parses it partly as a signature. Judging which occurrences are load-bearing requires reading what follows the formula, not the formula itself.

used_by.org: 国家互联网信息办公室 (CAC)
used_by.note: first substantive principle of the Global AI Governance Initiative
also used for new urbanisation in the 15th Five-Year Plan Recommendations and for talent policy in the 2016 innovation strategy

usage_examples.zh: 发展人工智能应坚持“以人为本”理念，以增进人类共同福祉为目标。
usage_examples.en: The development of AI should uphold the people-centred concept, with the goal of advancing the common wellbeing of humanity.

usage_examples.zh: 坚持创新驱动实质是人才驱动，落实以人为本，尊重创新创造的价值。
usage_examples.en: Innovation-driven development is in essence talent-driven; implement the people-centred principle and respect the value of innovation and creation.

definition_en: The set of actions and resources an agent is allowed to touch. Least privilege — granting only what the current task requires — is the central control for bounding agent behaviour.
definition_zh: 智能体被允许执行的操作和可访问的资源范围。最小权限原则（只授予当前任务所必需的权限）是约束智能体行为的核心手段。
pitfalls: 权限 (permissions/privileges) and 授权 (authorization, the act of granting) are cleanly distinguished in Chinese and should not be merged — 权限 is the noun for what you have, 授权 the verb/noun for granting it. The idiomatic Chinese for a violation is 越权操作 ('exceeding-authority operation'), which is more vivid than English 'unauthorized action' and is what PRC security writing uses about agents. 最小权限（原则）is the well-established rendering of least privilege, inherited from infosec, and transfers to agents without friction. Note that the newer English coinage 'least agency' has no Chinese equivalent; Chinese white papers that discuss it render it as 最小代理权, which reintroduces 代理.

translations.notes: Fully standard; 最小权限 = least privilege, 越权 = exceeding one's permissions.

definition_en: The property of a single neuron responding to several unrelated concepts, so that reading off 'what a neuron means' is impossible. The empirical symptom that superposition explains.
definition_zh: 同一个神经元会对多个毫不相关的概念做出反应，因此无法说清"这个神经元代表什么"。它是叠加现象在观测层面的表现。
pitfalls: Three renderings are in live use with no winner: 多义性 (borrowed from linguistics, where 多义词 = polysemous word — the closest analogue to the English coinage), 多语义(性) (a more literal poly-+semantic calque), and 多重语义 (descriptive, 'multiple semantics'). Because 多义性 is a pre-existing linguistics term, a Chinese reader may first think of lexical ambiguity rather than neuron overloading; conversely 多语义性 reads as a fresh technical coinage but is less idiomatic. The antonym is 单义性 / 单语义性 (monosemanticity), inheriting the same split.

translations.notes: Our recommendation: shortest, matches the linguistics term 多义词, and the antonym 单义性 works cleanly.

attestations.quote_zh: 这使得模型能够表示比神经元数量更多的概念，从而有效地逆转了导致单个神经元多义性的叠加现象。

definition_en: The tendency of a sufficiently capable goal-directed system to acquire resources, options and influence, and to resist being shut down or modified, because holding more power makes almost any goal easier to achieve.
definition_zh: 指足够强的目标导向系统倾向于获取资源、选项和影响力，并抵制被关闭或修改，因为掌握更多的支配力几乎有助于实现任何目标。
pitfalls: This is the most politically loaded term in the category. 权力 in PRC register means *political* power — state authority, office, rule — so 寻求权力 / 夺取权力 reads as an AI seeking to govern, which sounds like science fiction and is awkward to publish. Two independent sources visibly wobble on the word: the CCL 2023 survey writes 权利剥夺 and Chinese Wikipedia writes 权利夺取, both using 权利 ('rights') where 权力 ('power') is meant — a homophone slip that signals the term has not settled. Chinese discourse frequently sidesteps the noun entirely and describes the behaviour instead (获取更多计算资源, 寻求更多的影响力, 追求自我保持), which is why the concept is often present without a fixed name. 攫取权力 is available but connotes usurpation and is even more politically charged.

translations.notes: Recommended as the most neutral and transparent rendering, but no source located in this pass uses it as a settled technical term; Chinese writing prefers 夺取权力 or avoids the noun. Recorded as contested rather than established.
Chinese Wikipedia's choice. Stronger than the English — 夺取 implies wresting power away from someone, which imports a takeover framing into what is meant as a statistical tendency.

attestations.quote_zh: 一些人认为，这类先进的人工智能系统或许无可避免的带有从周围环境（包括人类在内）夺取权力的倾向

translations.pinyin: huòqǔ gèng duō zīyuán / xúnqiú gèng duō de yǐngxiǎnglì

This avoids the political register problem but means the concept has no citable headword. Only the 寻求更多的影响力 half is attested; a Chinese Wikipedia sentence previously filed here writes 获取更多计算资源, not 获取更多资源, and has been removed. Recorded in research as “获取更多资源 / 寻求更多的影响力”.

translations.notes: Attested but recommended against: 权利 means 'rights/entitlements', not 'power'. The intended word is 权力. definition_en: The doctrine that a designated entity — usually the platform or service provider — bears first-line, non-delegable responsibility for everything that happens on or through its service, including building the internal management systems, staffing, review procedures and technical measures needed to discharge it. It is not a rule about liability for a particular breach but a standing allocation of the governance burden: Article 7 of the Algorithmic Recommendation Provisions requires providers to 落实算法安全主体责任 and then lists the systems they must build (mechanism review, ethics review, user registration, publication review, data and personal-information protection, anti-fraud, security assessment and monitoring, incident response); Article 8 of the Network Information Content Ecosystem Governance Provisions imposes 信息内容管理主体责任 on content platforms; Article 9 of the Generative AI Interim Measures assigns providers responsibility as the producer of online information content.
definition_zh: 指特定主体（通常是平台或服务提供者）对其服务上发生的一切承担第一位、不可转移的责任，并须为此建立相应的管理制度、配备人员、设置审核程序和技术措施。它不是针对某一违法行为的责任分配，而是治理负担的常态性归属：《互联网信息服务算法推荐管理规定》第七条要求"落实算法安全主体责任"并列举须建立的各项制度；《网络信息内容生态治理规定》第八条规定平台"应当履行信息内容管理主体责任"；《生成式人工智能服务管理暂行办法》第九条要求提供者"依法承担网络信息内容生产者责任"。
pitfalls: English 'accountability' is the usual substitute and is materially weaker: accountability is answerability after the fact, whereas 主体责任 is an affirmative, continuous duty to construct and staff a compliance apparatus before anything goes wrong, plus strict attribution of whatever does. It is also not 'primary liability' in the tort sense — no plaintiff, no damages, no fault requirement; the counterparty is the regulator. Two further distortions: (a) 主体 means 'the entity that is the subject of the duty', so 主体责任 is closer to 'the responsibility that comes with being the responsible party' — a tautology in English but a precise allocation rule in Chinese; (b) the phrase originates in Party discipline discourse (党委主体责任) and carries the connotation that the responsibility sits with the organisation's leadership personally, which is why PRC rules pair it with named responsible-person requirements. Translating it as 'accountability' loses the note that a named human is on the hook.

en_renderings.notes: DigiChina's rendering ('fulfil their primary responsibility for algorithmic security'), and the form most English readers of translated PRC instruments will meet. Adequate but reads as a ranking ('primary vs secondary') rather than as an allocation to the responsible entity.

attestations.quote_zh: 算法推荐服务提供者应当落实算法安全主体责任，建立健全算法机制机理审核、科技伦理审查、用户注册、信息发布审核、数据安全和个人信息保护、反电信网络诈骗、安全评估监测、安全事件应急处置等管理制度和技术措施，制定并公开算法推荐服务相关规则，配备与算法推荐服务规模相适应的专业人员和技术支撑。
attestations.quote_en: Article 7: Algorithmic recommendation service providers shall: fulfil their primary responsibility for algorithmic security, establish and complete management systems and technical measures for algorithmic mechanism examination and verification, technology ethics review, user registration, information dissemination examination and verification, security assessment and monitoring, security incident response and handling, data security and personal information protection, countering telecommunications and online fraud …
attestations.source_title: Translation: Internet Information Service Algorithmic Recommendation Management Provisions (Article 7)
attestations.publisher: DigiChina, Stanford University (trans. Rogier Creemers, Graham Webster, Helen Toner)

en_renderings.notes: Preferred here as the database headword: 'principal' carries both senses the Chinese needs — the party that is principally responsible, and the party that is *the principal* rather than an agent or intermediary. Use with a gloss ('a standing duty to build and staff the compliance apparatus, not merely to answer for failures').

attestations.quote_zh: 网络信息内容服务平台应当履行信息内容管理主体责任，加强本平台网络信息内容生态治理，培育积极健康、向上向善的网络文化。
attestations.quote_en: Online information content service platforms shall discharge their principal responsibility for information content management, strengthen governance of the online information content ecosystem on their platform, and cultivate a positive, healthy and uplifting online culture.
attestations.source_title: 《网络信息内容生态治理规定》第八条
attestations.publisher: 国家互联网信息办公室 (Cyberspace Administration of China)

why_no_english: English distributes across at least four words what Chinese packs into two characters: 'accountability' (answerability), 'liability' (legal exposure to a claim), 'duty of care' (a standard of conduct owed to others) and 'compliance obligation' (a specific regulatory requirement). 主体责任 is none of these individually and all of them at once, plus something none of them has: an assignment of *who the responsible subject is*, made once and applied to every future obligation in the instrument. Because English has no word for it, translated PRC rules read as though they merely urge platforms to be responsible, when in Chinese they are naming the platform as the load-bearing party for the entire regulatory scheme — which is why so much PRC AI regulation can be written in one line ('the provider bears principal responsibility') and still bite.

definition_en: Training a small classifier on a model's frozen internal activations to test whether a given piece of information is linearly decodable from them.
definition_zh: 在冻结的模型内部激活上训练一个小分类器，用来检验某种信息是否能从这些激活中线性地读出来。
pitfalls: Two forms coexist without conflict: 探针 (the noun, 'probe' — used for the object, especially 线性探针 for a linear probe) and 探测 (the verb/gerund, 'probing' — used for the method). Both are pre-existing terms borrowed from instrumentation and are unproblematic. The only caution is that 探针 in Chinese biology/electronics means a physical probe, so a lay reader may picture hardware, but this is the same metaphor English uses.

translations.notes: Noun form. 线性探针 = linear probe is the standard collocation.

attestations.quote_zh: 梳理了包括因果归因（Causal Attribution）、探针（Probing）、梯度检测（Gradient Detection）等主流定位技术。
attestations.quote_en: It surveys mainstream localisation techniques including causal attribution, probing and gradient detection.

attestations.publisher: 机器之心 (via 腾讯云开发者社区)

translations.notes: Verb/method form, used in survey prose.

attestations.quote_zh: 探测（Probing）涉及训练一个小型分类器，以查看是否可以从内部向量中解码出特定概念。

attestations.publisher: alphaXiv 中文导读 (arXiv 2601.14004)

definition_en: Rewarding each step of a model's reasoning chain rather than only the final answer. Contrasted with outcome supervision; produces process reward models (PRMs) and is argued to be more alignment-friendly because it rewards a human-endorsed chain of reasoning, not just a correct output.
definition_zh: 对模型推理链条的每一步分别给予奖励，而不是只看最终答案对不对。与结果监督相对，训练出的是过程奖励模型（PRM）；由于它奖励的是人类认可的推理过程本身，通常被认为对对齐更友好。
pitfalls: The 过程监督 / 结果监督 pair is clean and stable; the main risk is the adjacent abbreviations PRM / ORM, which Chinese writers almost always leave in Latin letters (过程奖励模型（PRM）). Note also that 监督 here means supervision in the ML sense (as in 监督学习), not oversight in the governance sense — the same character string that renders 'oversight' in scalable-oversight.

translations.notes: Fixed by Chinese coverage of OpenAI's 'Let's Verify Step by Step' (2023) and reinforced by the o1/R1-era reasoning-model literature.

attestations.quote_zh: 过程监督相比结果监督有一个明显的优势，那就是它提供了比结果监督更精确的反馈
attestations.quote_en: Process supervision has one obvious advantage over outcome supervision: it provides more precise feedback.

definition_en: An attack in which adversarial instructions reach a model through its input channel — often indirectly, hidden in a web page, document or database the model reads — and are followed as if they came from the legitimate user.

zh_headword: 舆论属性或社会动员能力
pinyin: yúlùn shǔxìng huò shèhuì dòngyuán nénglì
en: public opinion attributes or social mobilisation capability
en_aliases: public opinion properties or social mobilization capabilities
public opinion properties or the capacity for social mobilization
definition_en: The statutory trigger phrase that pulls an internet service — including an algorithmic recommendation service, a deep synthesis service or a generative AI service — into the security assessment and algorithm filing regimes. The 2018 Provisions define it extensively rather than by test: it covers running forums, blogs, microblogs, chat rooms, messaging groups, public accounts, short video, livestreaming, information sharing or mini-programs (or adding such functions), plus any other internet information service that provides a channel for public expression of opinion or has the capacity to mobilise the public to undertake particular activities. In practice any consumer-facing service with a text output box is inside it.
definition_zh: 把一项互联网服务（含算法推荐、深度合成、生成式人工智能服务）拉入安全评估和算法备案制度的法定触发用语。《具有舆论属性或社会动员能力的互联网信息服务安全评估规定》第二条采取列举加兜底的定义方式：开办论坛、博客、微博客、聊天室、通讯群组、公众账号、短视频、网络直播、信息分享、小程序等信息服务或者附设相应功能；以及开办提供公众舆论表达渠道或者具有发动社会公众从事特定活动能力的其他互联网信息服务。实践中，任何面向公众、有文本输出的服务基本都落入其内。
preferred_zh: 舆论属性或社会动员能力
pitfalls: Do not translate the two limbs separately or paraphrase; it is a legal term of art that must travel as a unit, like 'reasonable expectation of privacy'. 舆论 is not 'public opinion' in the polling sense — it is closer to 'the circulating discourse of the public', an object that can be guided, and the regulation treats a service's capacity to *host or shape* it as the regulated attribute. 社会动员能力 sounds sinister in English ('mobilisation') but names an ordinary technical property: the ability of a platform to get many people to do the same thing at once. Read literally, the phrase looks like a narrow carve-out for political services; read as PRC regulators read it, it is the near-universal jurisdictional hook, and treating it as narrow is the most common analytical error English readers make about how much of China's AI sector is inside the filing regime. Also note the phrase recurs almost verbatim, with a variant wording, in the Sci-Tech Ethics Review Measures' review-recheck list ('具有舆论社会动员能力和社会意识引导能力的算法模型').

en_renderings.en: public opinion properties or social mobilization capabilities
en_renderings.notes: DigiChina's wording, the most widely propagated English form. China Law Translate's variant 'public opinion properties or the capacity for social mobilization' is equally common. British-spelling 'public opinion attributes or social mobilisation capability' is used here as the headword; all three refer to the same statutory phrase and should be treated as one term.

attestations.quote_zh: 本规定所称具有舆论属性或社会动员能力的互联网信息服务，包括下列情形：（一）开办论坛、博客、微博客、聊天室、通讯群组、公众账号、短视频、网络直播、信息分享、小程序等信息服务或者附设相应功能；（二）开办提供公众舆论表达渠道或者具有发动社会公众从事特定活动能力的其他互联网信息服务。
attestations.quote_en: 'Internet information services with public opinion attributes or social mobilisation capability' as used in these Provisions include the following: (1) operating forums, blogs, microblogs, chat rooms, messaging groups, public accounts, short video, livestreaming, information sharing, mini-programs and other such information services, or adding corresponding functions; (2) operating other internet information services that provide channels for the public expression of opinion or that have the capacity to mobilise the public to engage in particular activities.
attestations.source_title: 《具有舆论属性或社会动员能力的互联网信息服务安全评估规定》第二条
attestations.publisher: 国家互联网信息办公室、公安部

attestations.quote_zh: 具有舆论属性或者社会动员能力的算法推荐服务提供者应当在提供服务之日起十个工作日内通过互联网信息服务算法备案系统填报……履行备案手续。
attestations.quote_en: Providers of algorithmic recommendation services with public opinion properties or having social mobilization capabilities shall, within 10 working days of providing services, report … through the Internet information service algorithm filing system, and carry out filing formalities.
attestations.source_title: Translation: Internet Information Service Algorithmic Recommendation Management Provisions (Article 24)
attestations.publisher: DigiChina, Stanford University (trans. Rogier Creemers, Graham Webster, Helen Toner)

why_no_english: English regulatory drafting delimits scope by counting things — user numbers, revenue, compute, systemic-risk designation. This phrase delimits scope by a *qualitative social property*: whether a service can carry public discourse or set many people in motion. There is no English legal term for that property, because no Anglophone regime uses it as a jurisdictional hook. Rendering it word by word produces an English phrase that sounds like a narrow political-media category, when in operation it is the broadest possible net — so the translation is simultaneously literal and misleading. The phrase also encodes, in six characters, the premise that shaping public discourse is the regulated harm; an English reader without that premise cannot reconstruct why filing, assessment, real-name verification and content controls all hang off the same trigger.

usage_examples.en: Where deep synthesis service providers develop and launch new products, applications or functions with public opinion attributes or social mobilisation capability, they shall carry out a security assessment in accordance with relevant state provisions.

definition_en: A dynamic in which competing developers or jurisdictions progressively cut safety investment because whoever spends least moves fastest, so caution is punished by the market or by rivals.
definition_zh: 指相互竞争的开发者或司法辖区不断削减安全投入，因为谁在安全上花得最少谁跑得最快，于是谨慎反而被市场或对手惩罚。
pitfalls: 逐底竞争 is a well-established Chinese term, but it arrived from trade and labour economics (jurisdictions cutting wages, taxes or environmental standards to attract capital), and that is still where its centre of gravity sits; attestations located in this pass are about regulatory and market competition rather than about AI labs cutting safety work specifically. The variant 竞次 is a compact, more literary synonym. Separately, Chinese AI-risk writing very often reaches for 军备竞赛 ('arms race') instead — a different and stronger metaphor that frames the problem as state-versus-state rivalry rather than as a collective-action failure among firms, and that carries geopolitical charge in PRC register. Choose deliberately: 逐底竞争 for 'everyone cuts corners', 军备竞赛 for 'nations race'.

translations.notes: Established Chinese economics term now applied to AI regulation and AI markets. Attestation located is Chinese media coverage of AI regulatory dynamics rather than an AI-safety source, so recorded as common rather than established in this field.

attestations.quote_zh: 逐底竞争
attestations.quote_en: race to the bottom
attestations.source_title: 《美国AI监管急转：从“防守型监管”全面转向“进攻型去监管”》
attestations.publisher: 网易 (163.com)

translations.notes: Compact synonym of 逐底竞争, current in Chinese economics writing. No AI-specific attestation located in this pass.

The metaphor Chinese AI-risk writing most often reaches for. Not a synonym — it frames the dynamic as inter-state rivalry rather than as competitive erosion of standards — but recorded because it is what readers will encounter.

attestations.quote_zh: 一些学者将当前的人工智能竞赛比作冷战时期的军备竞赛
attestations.quote_en: Some scholars compare the current AI race to the arms race of the Cold War era.
attestations.source_title: 《人工智能安全》
attestations.publisher: 维基百科（中文）

usage_examples.zh: 如果监管放松引发逐底竞争，安全投入最少的公司反而跑得最快。
usage_examples.en: If deregulation triggers a race to the bottom, the company investing least in safety ends up moving fastest.

definition_en: The general PRC requirement that users of network services be identified to the operator by verified real identity before receiving service. Article 24 of the Cybersecurity Law obliges network operators to require real identity information when signing an agreement or confirming service for network access, domain registration, phone activation, information publishing or instant messaging, and forbids them from serving users who do not supply it. For AI services the duty is specified in Article 9 of the Deep Synthesis Provisions, which requires verification by mobile number, ID document number, unified social credit code or the national online identity authentication public service, and bars unverified users from information-publishing functions. The result is that Chinese consumer AI services are, as a matter of law, non-anonymous at the account layer.
definition_zh: 网络服务用户须经真实身份验证方可获得服务的普遍性制度。《网络安全法》第二十四条规定，网络运营者为用户办理网络接入、域名注册、入网手续，或者提供信息发布、即时通讯等服务时，应当要求用户提供真实身份信息，用户不提供的不得为其提供相关服务。人工智能领域由《互联网信息服务深度合成管理规定》第九条具体化：应基于移动电话号码、身份证件号码、统一社会信用代码或者国家网络身份认证公共服务等方式进行真实身份信息认证，未认证者不得提供信息发布服务。
pitfalls: 'Real-name system' is a calque that has stuck, but it invites two misreadings. First, it is not KYC: KYC is a financial-crime control owed to a financial regulator and centres on beneficial ownership and sanctions screening; 实名制 is a content-attribution control owed to the cyberspace and public security authorities, and its purpose is that any published item can be traced to a natural person. Second, 'real name' overstates the display requirement — Chinese services are 后台实名、前台自愿 (real name on the back end, chosen display name on the front end), so users still appear under handles. Note also the practical AI consequence English coverage rarely draws: because 实名制 attaches to information *publishing*, the binding version of the rule for an LLM service is not 'you must give your ID to chat' but 'you must give your ID before anything you generate can be posted', and it makes anonymous public red-teaming of Chinese consumer models structurally impossible.

en_renderings.notes: The near-universal English form in policy writing and media. Recommended, with a one-clause gloss on first use ('back-end identity verification; front-end pseudonyms remain permitted').

attestations.quote_zh: 网络运营者为用户办理网络接入、域名注册服务，办理固定电话、移动电话等入网手续，或者为用户提供信息发布、即时通讯等服务，在与用户签订协议或者确认提供服务时，应当要求用户提供真实身份信息。用户不提供真实身份信息的，网络运营者不得为其提供相关服务。
attestations.quote_en: Network operators handling network access and domain registration services for users, handling network activation procedures for stationary or mobile phones, or providing users with services for publishing information or instant messaging, shall require users to provide real identity information when signing agreements with the users or confirming the provision of services. Where users do not provide real identity information, network operators must not provide them with the relevant services.
attestations.source_title: 《中华人民共和国网络安全法》第二十四条 / PRC Cybersecurity Law, Article 24
attestations.publisher: 全国人大常委会; English translation by China Law Translate

attestations.quote_zh: 深度合成服务提供者应当基于移动电话号码、身份证件号码、统一社会信用代码或者国家网络身份认证公共服务等方式，依法对深度合成服务使用者进行真实身份信息认证，不得向未进行真实身份信息认证的深度合成服务使用者提供信息发布服务。
attestations.quote_en: Deep synthesis service providers shall lawfully verify the real identity information of deep synthesis service users by means such as mobile phone number, ID document number, unified social credit code, or the national online identity authentication public service, and must not provide information-publishing services to users who have not completed real identity verification.
attestations.source_title: 《互联网信息服务深度合成管理规定》第九条
attestations.publisher: 中国政府网 (State Council)

en_renderings.notes: The wording that appears when the statutes are translated clause by clause (真实身份信息 / 真实身份信息认证). More precise than 'real-name system' for the operative duty, and preferable when translating a specific article; 'real-name system' is better for the regime as a whole.

attestations.quote_zh: 在与用户签订协议或者确认提供服务时，应当要求用户提供真实身份信息。用户不提供真实身份信息的，网络运营者不得为其提供相关服务。
attestations.quote_en: … shall require users to provide real identity information when signing agreements with the users or confirming the provision of services. Where users do not provide real identity information, network operators must not provide them with the relevant services.
attestations.source_title: PRC Cybersecurity Law, Article 24
attestations.publisher: China Law Translate

why_no_english: English has 'identity verification', 'KYC' and 'age verification', each tied to a purpose (fraud, finance, child protection). 实名制 is purpose-agnostic and society-wide: a standing legal presumption that network activity is attributable, applied uniformly across telecoms, platforms, messaging and now AI services, and enforced by denial of service rather than by penalty. English lacks a noun for 'a general regime of compulsory attributability', so 'real-name system' is a calque that carries the words without the systemic weight — and it actively misleads on the front-end/back-end split, since Anglophone 'real-name policies' (e.g. historical platform rules) meant display names, the opposite of PRC practice.

used_by.note: 'real identity information' in the Cybersecurity Law translation

usage_examples.zh: 未完成实名认证的用户无法使用该模型的内容发布功能。
usage_examples.en: Users who have not completed real-name verification cannot use the model's content publishing function.

definition_en: A model trained (usually with RL on verifiable tasks) to produce extended internal reasoning before answering — o1, DeepSeek-R1, Qwen3 thinking mode. Distinguished from a chat model by spending far more output tokens on deliberation.
definition_zh: 经过训练（通常是在可验证任务上做强化学习）后，会在回答前先进行长篇内部推理的模型，例如 o1、DeepSeek-R1、Qwen3 的思考模式。与普通对话模型的区别在于把大量输出 token 花在思考上。
pitfalls: The single worst ambiguity in this category. Chinese 推理 covers BOTH English senses: (a) reasoning — logical inference, deliberation; and (b) inference — the forward pass, serving, deployment. They are unrelated concepts in English engineering vocabulary but one word in Chinese. So 推理模型 can mean 'reasoning model' (o1-like), 推理引擎 means 'inference engine' (vLLM), 推理速度 means 'inference speed', and 推理能力 means 'reasoning ability'. OpenRLHF's Chinese README contains both senses within a few lines of each other. LLaMA-Factory's Chinese README uses 推理 for inference throughout, then writes 推理 / 非推理两个版本 meaning reasoning / non-reasoning model variants. There is no disambiguating convention; readers rely entirely on context. When precision matters, write 推理（reasoning）模型 or use 思考模型 / 慢思考模型 for the reasoning sense and 部署 / 服务 / 前向推理 to force the inference sense. Chinese labs partly sidestep this by branding the behaviour 思考模式 (thinking mode) rather than calling the model a 推理模型.

translations.notes: The dominant rendering despite the ambiguity. Also 大型推理模型 / 大推理模型 (LRM) in survey translations, and 推理大模型 in Chinese media.

attestations.quote_zh: 使用 REINFORCE++-baseline 通过长期 RL 训练训练最先进的 1.5B 推理模型。

definition_en: Leike et al.'s scheme in which a reward model is trained with the help of AI assistants that were themselves trained by reward modelling, recursively bootstrapping supervision up to tasks humans cannot evaluate unaided.

definition_en: An AI system improving its own cognitive machinery, so that gains in capability feed back into the ability to make further gains. The proposed mechanism behind an intelligence explosion.
definition_zh: 指人工智能系统改进自身的认知机制，使能力提升反过来增强其继续提升能力的本事，从而形成正反馈。这被认为是智能爆炸的实现机制。
pitfalls: Contested, and the competing renderings differ in more than style. 递归自我改进 / 递归式自我改进 preserve the recursion, which is the whole content of the concept. But the official register sidesteps recursion entirely: the Chinese International AI Safety Report renders OpenAI's 'AI self-improvement' capability category as 人工智能自我提升能力, and Chinese media commonly reach for 自我迭代 or 自我演化, all of which describe a system getting better over time without the load-bearing claim that the improvement process improves itself. Note also that the abbreviation RSI is used bare in Chinese text, which is often the cleanest option. 改进 vs 提升: 改进 (improve/modify) fits rewriting one's own algorithms; 提升 (raise/elevate) fits benchmark scores.

translations.notes: The rendering used when the recursion is the point. Attested with an explicit definition in Chinese business media, which also uses the bare abbreviation RSI alongside it.

attestations.quote_zh: 所谓递归自我改进，就是AI介入对其自身的改进，从而形成“能力提升—研发能力增强—能力进一步提升”的正反馈。
attestations.quote_en: So-called recursive self-improvement means AI intervening in its own improvement, forming a positive feedback loop of 'capability gain — stronger R&D capability — further capability gain'.

definition_en: Behaviours or capabilities that no AI system may ever exhibit, framed as absolute and non-negotiable prohibitions rather than risk trade-offs. The IDAIS Beijing statement (2024) proposed self-replication, power-seeking, WMD assistance and persistent deception as candidate red lines.
definition_zh: 任何 AI 系统在任何情况下都不得逾越的行为或能力边界，是绝对禁止而非风险权衡。2024 年 IDAIS 北京共识把自主复制、权力寻求、协助制造大规模杀伤性武器和持续欺骗列为候选红线。
pitfalls: This is the rare case where Chinese is STRONGER than English, and that itself is the pitfall. 红线 is deeply entrenched in PRC political language — 生态保护红线, 耕地红线, 不可逾越的红线 — where it denotes a hard, state-declared, non-negotiable limit, often with sovereignty or national-security overtones. So the technical AI-safety sense arrives pre-legitimised: a Chinese policy reader hears 'inviolable state-backed boundary', which is roughly the rhetorical force IDAIS wanted, and this is very likely why the red-lines framing gained traction in China faster than most imported AI-safety vocabulary. The risk is the reverse of the usual one: the term may be MORE load-bearing in Chinese than the underlying technical consensus supports, and 红线 can slide from 'capability threshold' into 'political line'. Note the 上海共识 gloss 「高压线」 (high-voltage line), which sharpens the sense of an automatic, physical consequence for crossing. Distinguish from 底线 (bottom line/minimum standard), which is weaker and more negotiable.

translations.notes: Used as the headline term in both the IDAIS Beijing consensus (2024) and the IDAIS-linked 上海共识 (2025). Both documents exist in authoritative Chinese, so this is a source-language usage, not a translation.

usage_examples.en: No AI system should be able to copy or improve itself without explicit human approval and assistance.

usage_examples.en: We need comprehensive governance mechanisms to ensure that systems developed or deployed do not violate the red lines.

definition_en: The two-tier risk-threshold design of the Shanghai AI Lab / Concordia AI Frontier AI Risk Management Framework. A 红线 (red line) is an intolerable-harm threshold that must not be crossed; a 黄线 (yellow line) is an early-warning threshold on the enabling capabilities and propensities that would make a red-line path viable. Results are sorted into a green / yellow / red zone, which determines whether a model gets routine deployment, controlled deployment, or suspension of deployment or development.
definition_zh: 《前沿人工智能风险管理框架》提出的双层风险阈值机制。“红线”是不可容忍的危害阈值，一旦触发即应暂停部署或开发；“黄线”是前瞻性预警指标，标示关键使能能力、行为倾向或防护缺失等前置条件。二者共同把模型划入绿区、黄区或红区，直接决定部署决策。
pitfalls: Three things go wrong in translation. (1) 红线 is a heavily loaded PRC political idiom for a non-negotiable limit (territorial red lines, ecological 生态保护红线); English 'red line' carries diplomatic-ultimatum connotations instead of the regulatory-threshold sense, and readers may hear rhetoric where the document means an auditable trigger. (2) The pair is routinely collapsed: English coverage reports 'China's AI red lines' and drops 黄线 entirely, which destroys the mechanism — the yellow line is where the framework does its actual anticipatory work, because a red line only fires once a credible harm pathway already exists. (3) Do not equate the scheme with ASL levels or preparedness tiers: it is not an ordered capability ladder. Each red line is an independent threshold defined over a deployment-environment / threat-source / enabling-capability (ETC) triple, and the framework says explicitly that the numbering (CY1–CY3, B1–B3) does not encode severity or progression. Also note the framework calls red lines developer 自我约束 pending consensus, not regulation.

en_renderings.notes: The framework's own English title is 'Frontier AI Risk Management Framework', and the threshold pair is normally rendered literally. Keep both terms; dropping 'yellow line' loses the mechanism.

attestations.quote_zh: 本框架通过划定“红线”（不应逾越的不可容忍阈值）和“黄线”（潜在风险的早期预警指标）来设定人工智能的安全边界
attestations.quote_en: This framework sets AI safety boundaries by drawing 'red lines' (intolerable thresholds that must not be crossed) and 'yellow lines' (early-warning indicators of potential risk).
attestations.source_title: 《前沿人工智能风险管理框架 2.0》
attestations.publisher: 上海人工智能实验室 / 安远 AI (Concordia AI)

attestations.quote_zh: 我们建议开发者为风险界定不可容忍的阈值（“红线”）和早期预警指标（“黄线”），将理论化的描述转化为便于实操的决策标准。
attestations.quote_en: We recommend that developers define intolerable thresholds ('red lines') and early-warning indicators ('yellow lines') for risks, turning theoretical descriptions into operable decision criteria.
attestations.source_title: 《前沿人工智能风险管理框架 2.0》
attestations.publisher: 上海人工智能实验室 / 安远 AI (Concordia AI)

en_renderings.literal_back: green zone / yellow zone / red zone
en_renderings.notes: The companion concept (绿区/黄区/红区) that the thresholds sort models into. Translating the lines without the zones leaves the consequences invisible: yellow zone means controlled deployment, red zone means suspension.

attestations.quote_zh: 三类风险区分别为：绿区（常规部署、广泛可接受）、黄区（受控部署、严格管控下可容忍）或红区（暂停部署或开发、不可接受）。
attestations.quote_en: The three risk zones are: green zone (routine deployment, broadly acceptable), yellow zone (controlled deployment, tolerable under strict controls), and red zone (suspend deployment or development, unacceptable).
attestations.source_title: 《前沿人工智能风险管理框架 2.0》
attestations.publisher: 上海人工智能实验室 / 安远 AI (Concordia AI)

why_no_english: English frontier-safety design converged on ordered capability ladders — ASL levels, preparedness tiers, capability thresholds — in which a single scale is climbed and each rung attaches a mitigation package. The 红线/黄线 scheme is a genuinely different shape: two qualitatively distinct kinds of threshold (an intolerable-outcome line and a precursor line), each instantiated independently per risk domain over an environment–threat–capability triple, feeding a three-zone deployment decision. English has 'threshold' and 'tripwire' but no established paired vocabulary for 'the line you must never cross' versus 'the line that tells you the crossing is becoming possible', and no term for a threshold defined over a context triple rather than over a capability score. Translating the words is easy; the reason the entry matters is that an English reader will file it as 'China's version of ASL' and miss that it is an alternative architecture — one that is deliberately interoperable with TC260 2.0 and the EU Code of Practice, as the framework's own mapping appendices set out.

used_by.org: 上海人工智能实验室 / 安远 AI (Concordia AI)
used_by.note: Originating framework; §2.1 defines both, §2.2 instantiates red lines for cyber, bio, chemical, persuasion and loss-of-control risks.
Reported the 1.0 release, describing the framework as turning risks from '模糊的定义' into '精确的坐标'.

usage_examples.zh: 已越过黄线或红线的人工智能模型，至少应满足三级（监督保护级）的等级保护要求。
usage_examples.en: AI models that have crossed a yellow line or a red line should at minimum meet Level 3 (supervisory protection) requirements of the graded protection scheme.

usage_examples.zh: 当红线被触发时，我们建议模型开发者立即采取措施，阻断潜在灾难性后果的发生路径。
usage_examples.en: When a red line is triggered, we recommend that model developers immediately take measures to block the pathway to the potential catastrophic outcome.

definition_en: A structured exercise in which people or automated systems deliberately play the adversary against a model or system in order to surface vulnerabilities, harmful behaviours and misuse pathways before real attackers find them.
definition_zh: 由人员或自动化系统扮演攻击方，对模型或系统发起有组织的对抗测试，以在真实攻击者之前发现漏洞、有害行为和滥用路径。
pitfalls: The colour convention is worth checking but did NOT turn out to be a live problem. In PLA exercise convention 红军 is the friendly/home force and 蓝军 the opposing force — the inverse of the US convention. However, Chinese AI and cybersecurity writing uses the 红队/蓝队 (team) pair, not the 红军/蓝军 (army) pair, and in that pair 红队 is uniformly the attacker and 蓝队 the defender, matching the US usage. We found no instance of a Chinese AI-safety text treating 红队 as the defending side, and no instance of an author flagging confusion. Treat the inversion as a fact about the military register only. Two secondary notes: (a) 红队测试 in the PRC arrives via the mature 攻防演练 (attack-defence exercise) industry, so it carries strong infosec/pen-test connotations and a Chinese reader may under-read the AI-safety sense of probing for harmful content and misaligned behaviour rather than exploitable bugs; (b) 红队演练 is used interchangeably with 红队测试.

translations.notes: The dominant form across AI-safety, policy and industry security writing. 红队 alone is used as the noun for the team.

attestations.quote_zh: 红队测试（Red-teaming）：一种系统化的流程，其中专职人员或团队通过多种方法寻找漏洞、局限性或潜在的滥用风险。
attestations.quote_en: Red-teaming: a systematic process in which dedicated individuals or teams use a variety of methods to look for vulnerabilities, limitations or potential misuse risks.
attestations.source_title: 《2026年国际人工智能安全报告》（中文版）
attestations.publisher: International AI Safety Report（国际人工智能安全报告专家组）

attestations.quote_zh: ●领域专家红队测试：由领域专家通过模拟攻击或关键性挑战对AI模型进行对抗测试，主动识别潜在漏洞、新兴风险及安全改进空间。
attestations.quote_en: Domain-expert red-teaming: domain experts conduct adversarial testing of the AI model through simulated attacks or critical challenges, proactively identifying potential vulnerabilities, emerging risks and room for safety improvement.
attestations.source_title: 《人工智能前沿风险管理框架（1.0版）》
attestations.publisher: 上海人工智能实验室 / 安远AI (Concordia AI)

attestations.quote_zh: 智能体红队测试不是单次提示词越狱，而是系统化、场景化、多轮次、可复现的对抗性测试，核心遵循“侦察→建模→分层攻击→验证→报告→加固→复测”闭环流程，区别于传统软件红队，重点突出智能体自主性、上下文依赖、工具权限、记忆特性四大维度。
attestations.quote_en: Agent red-teaming is not a one-off prompt jailbreak but systematic, scenario-based, multi-turn, reproducible adversarial testing, following a closed loop of recon → modelling → layered attack → verification → reporting → hardening → retest; unlike traditional software red-teaming it foregrounds agent autonomy, context dependence, tool permissions and memory.
attestations.source_title: 面向AI智能体的红队测试实战：基于OWASP ASI 2026的金融场景攻防实践
attestations.publisher: 虎符智库，发表于安全内参

translations.notes: Preferred where the emphasis is on a staged exercise rather than a test procedure; inherited from 攻防演练.

attestations.quote_zh: 落实最佳实践并定期更新：五家公司都采用了一系列安全实践来落实各自框架，如开展内部和/或外部红队演练、激励第三方报告漏洞、加强对模型权重的网络安全和内部人员威胁防范等。
attestations.quote_en: Implementing and regularly updating best practice: all five companies adopt a range of safety practices to operationalise their frameworks, such as running internal and/or external red-team exercises, incentivising third-party vulnerability reporting, and strengthening cybersecurity and insider-threat defences for model weights.
attestations.source_title: 国际五大前沿AI风险管理框架的横向对比
attestations.publisher: 安远AI (Concordia AI)，发表于安全内参

translations.notes: Counterpart term, recorded here as evidence on the colour-convention question: in Chinese AI/cyber usage 蓝队 is the defender, i.e. the same way round as the US convention and the opposite of the PLA 红军/蓝军 arrangement.

attestations.quote_zh: 在攻防演练中，一个团队（红队）扮演攻击者的角色，试图发起各种攻击，而另一个团队（蓝队）则扮演防御者的角色，负责检测、阻止和应对攻击。
attestations.quote_en: In an attack-defence exercise, one team (the red team) plays the attacker and attempts various attacks, while the other team (the blue team) plays the defender and is responsible for detecting, blocking and responding to attacks.
attestations.source_title: 什么是攻防演练
attestations.publisher: 深信服 Sangfor 知识中心

usage_examples.en: All the companies conduct red-teaming during model development, and where possible invite independent third parties to run safety evaluations.

definition_en: A model declining to answer a request on safety grounds, and the training that produces this behaviour. The associated failure mode is over-refusal: declining legitimate requests because of surface triggers.
definition_zh: 模型出于安全考虑不回答某个请求，以及为产生这种行为所做的训练。对应的失效模式是过度拒答——因为触发了关键词就把正当请求也挡掉。
pitfalls: None problematic — this is a rare case where Chinese has a more compact and more usable term than English. 拒答 is a native two-character coinage that nominalises cleanly (拒答率 refusal rate, 过度拒答 over-refusal, 拒答数据 refusal data), where English needs 'refusal to answer'. Note that in Chinese industry usage 拒答 is framed primarily as a product defect to be minimised (降低拒答率), not as a safety property to be maximised — the register is closer to 'the model stonewalled the user' than to 'the model correctly refused'.

translations.notes: Fully established across Chinese lab, industry and security-research writing. Nominalises freely: 拒答率, 拒答数据, 拒答话术, 过度拒答.

attestations.quote_zh: 降低大模型拒答率，并支持对风险问题进行正向引导与纠偏
attestations.quote_en: Lower the model's refusal rate while supporting positive guidance and correction on risky questions.

definition_en: An imported governance instrument — a bounded environment in which an innovative service may be tested under relaxed or tailored regulatory conditions and supervisory observation. The term entered Chinese policy vocabulary through fintech (the PBoC's fintech innovation regulation pilots from 2019) and appears in PRC AI discourse mainly in two registers: as a policy recommendation, where CAICT proposes piloting sandbox regulation for innovative applications in qualified regions, specifying that application procedures, testing periods, risk monitoring, liability exemptions and dispute resolution would need to be defined; and as a deployment control in frontier-risk frameworks, where a regulatory sandbox is named as one of the controlled environments to which deployment of a yellow-zone model may be restricted. Notably, the same word is used in Chinese analysis to describe the EU AI Act sandboxes, which are the concrete reference case.
definition_zh: 外来治理工具：在受限环境中，对创新服务放宽或定制监管条件并由监管方观察其运行。该词经金融科技（2019年起人民银行金融科技创新监管试点）进入中国政策语汇，在人工智能语境中主要有两种用法。一是政策建议：中国信通院提出"对有望推动人工智能取得突破性进展与发展的创新应用，在有条件的区域试点'监管沙盒'，明确监管沙盒的申请流程、测试期限、风险监测、责任豁免及争议解决等核心机制"。二是部署管控措施：前沿风险框架把"监管沙盒"列为黄区模型可受限部署的受控环境之一。中文文献同时用该词描述欧盟《人工智能法》的沙盒制度，后者是主要参照对象。
pitfalls: The word translates trivially; what does not travel is its status. In English-language commentary 'China's regulatory sandbox for AI' is sometimes reported as though a national scheme exists. On the evidence gathered here it does not: CAICT's January 2026 governance report still frames it in the imperative-recommendation register ('pilot in qualified regions', 'define the application process, testing period, risk monitoring, liability exemptions and dispute resolution'), which is how PRC policy documents describe things that are not yet in place, and the report's concrete sandbox examples are Spanish, French and EU. Note also the word-order variant 沙盒监管 ('sandbox regulation'), used interchangeably. A second and quite different usage — sandbox as a *containment* environment for a high-risk model, alongside closed testing and qualified industry users — appears in the Shanghai AI Lab / Concordia frontier framework; this is closer to the engineering sense of sandboxing (cf. 沙箱) than to the regulatory instrument, and the two senses sit in the same paragraph in some documents.

en_renderings.notes: A direct calque of the English original, which is where the term came from; there is no independent Chinese coinage and no translation problem. Record it as a loanword travelling back. When writing about PRC AI policy, always state whether a given sandbox is proposed, locally piloted, or a foreign scheme being described — the Chinese term itself does not distinguish.

attestations.quote_zh: 一是推行创新场景"沙盒监管"试点。对有望推动人工智能取得突破性进展与发展的创新应用，在有条件的区域试点"监管沙盒"，明确监管沙盒的申请流程、测试期限、风险监测、责任豁免及争议解决等核心机制，在沙盒运营、运维、安全保障、跨机构协调等方面，建立规范管理体系。
attestations.quote_en: First, roll out 'sandbox regulation' pilots for innovative scenarios. For innovative applications with the potential to drive breakthrough progress in AI, pilot a 'regulatory sandbox' in qualified regions, defining core mechanisms such as the application process, testing period, risk monitoring, liability exemptions and dispute resolution, and establish a management system covering sandbox operation, maintenance, security assurance and cross-agency coordination.

why_no_english: This entry is the exception in the set: there is no English gap, because the concept is English in origin and the Chinese is a calque. What does not survive the round trip is the term's *modality*. In PRC policy prose, 监管沙盒 sits overwhelmingly in the recommendation and pilot register rather than the operative one, and it doubles as the word for a containment environment in frontier-safety documents. An English reader encountering 'regulatory sandbox' in a translated Chinese document has no cue that it may denote something proposed rather than existing, or a technical isolation environment rather than a regulatory relief scheme. The right move in English is therefore not a new word but a mandatory qualifier.

definition_en: Training a policy by having it act, receive a scalar reward, and update toward higher expected reward. In LLM post-training it is the stage that turns a fine-tuned model into one optimised against a reward model or a verifier.

pitfalls: None as a translation. Worth noting only that the bare Latin "RL" is extremely common in Chinese practitioner text as a modifier (RL 训练, RL 算法, RL 阶段), even though 强化学习 is a fully settled textbook term — the abbreviation is used for brevity, not because the Chinese is unavailable.

translations.notes: Textbook-stable since long before LLMs; used identically in classical RL, robotics and LLM post-training. No competing rendering.

definition_en: Post-training a language model against a reward model fitted to human preference comparisons. The canonical InstructGPT/ChatGPT alignment recipe: SFT, then reward modelling, then PPO.

pitfalls: The Chinese expansion exists in at least three word orders — 人类反馈强化学习, 基于人类反馈的强化学习, 从人类反馈中强化学习 — with no winner, precisely because nobody actually says them. The abbreviation RLHF is what circulates; the Chinese expansion appears once in parentheses as a gloss and then disappears. Treat the Chinese form as an explanatory apposition, not a usable term.

translations.notes: Overwhelmingly dominant. Even a project whose own name is Chinese-documented (OpenRLHF) writes RLHF 框架, RLHF 流程, RLHF 训练 throughout, glossing it in Chinese only in the opening sentence.

definition_en: RL in which the reward comes from a programmatic verifier — a unit test, an exact-match answer checker, a format validator — rather than a learned reward model. The DeepSeek-R1 / Tülu 3 era recipe for training reasoning models.
definition_zh: 奖励信号不来自学出来的奖励模型，而来自可以程序化判定的验证器：数学答案是否匹配、代码是否通过单元测试、输出格式是否合规。这是 DeepSeek-R1、Tülu 3 这一代推理模型的主流后训练做法。
pitfalls: Recent enough that the Chinese expansion is still unstable: 可验证奖励的强化学习 and 基于可验证奖励的强化学习 both circulate, and the abbreviation dominates both. Despite Chinese labs (DeepSeek, Moonshot) being central to the technique, the term itself was coined in English (Tülu 3) and Chinese sources import it — so this is NOT a case of Chinese being the source language.

translations.notes: Working form in Chinese technical writing. The Chinese expansion appears in parentheses on first mention.

attestations.quote_en: It was formally named RLVR (reinforcement learning based on verifiable rewards) in Tülu 3; its core idea is to replace the learned reward model with a programmatic verifier.
